Also, be prepared that it is cash only up to $30. There is an  ATM for convenience in the back of the location for a $1 fee.  All drinks are bottled products but there is a great variety.

The food is very good. Enjoyed a cheesesteak with fried onions. Steaks traditionally come with mayo and ketchup which I am high on both for a Philly steak. The sandwich is a great size, is delicious and sits perfectly on a slightly toasted roll that does a great job to keep all the steak kept inside of the roll. 

Also tried a chicken shish tawook sandwich which was delicious. It is like a halal cart platter wrapped in a pita. Also available on a long roll.

The interior is dated and the seating gives off an '80s feel but the staff is very helpfu

This was one of the best meals I had during the 4 years I went to school in Philly.  I saved it for my senior year, and it was well worth the wait.  The service was impeccable, and the food itself was amazing.  I was temporarily overwhelmed by the variety and couldn't decide if I wanted to take the sweet or savory brunch route.  Luckily the buffet setup allows you to do a little of both.

The place was a little more quiet and formal than I'm usually comfortable with, but who cares when you have such a great brunch spread before you?

I do not know why this restaurant doesn't have 5 stars or at least 4. This is a staple in the Chinatown community. Tell me somewhere else to eat for dim sum and I might judge you. They actually own Tom's too which I know other people go to but if you want a true, quality, and authentic experience of a family dim sum place, this is your place. They have the traditional clothed tables with the carts being pushed around. They also have tea typically served and make sure to tell them if you want the tea or not or there will be an upcharge as usual. I do not know what to recommend since it's in a different language and I cannot be bothered to translate but if it looks good on the cart while its passing or smells good, just get it. They take card but try to bring cash. They have wonderful service there and if there's something that you want that's NOT on the cart, just ask and they'll try to m

Called and placed an order for take out. We ordered a small pizza and baked ziti. They told us it would take 30 mins. We got there in 35 mins and it was all still in the oven so we had to wait. 

The pizza was really good. I would definitely get it again but it was that good that I would crave it. It was very greasy which I didn't like. 

The baked ziti only had cheese on the top so once that first layer was eaten it was honestly just red sauce and noodles. They definitely should put more cheese through the ziti.

Little Thai Market was... alright. I can't really say anything great about the place, but I can't really place my finger on anything bad either. 

After scoping out some places I wanted to try in Philadelphia for a work trip, Little Thai Market popped up. The reviews were raving about the salmon curry, which piqued my interest as I normally don't venture into seafood based curries. Upon arriving at the Reading Market, there was a long line in front that I was willing to stand in. They give you two options for your base on the curry dish, either rice with a garnish of broccoli, or all broccoli. I decided to go with the standard of all rice so I could let all the flavors come through the dish.

A very haggard employee took my order as he was helping to heat the salmon, grill the salmon, and fill the plates with orders. He came off as slightly rude, but I didn't hold this against him as he

Possibly the most genuinely nice and polite staff in Philadelphia!  The food is also quite good.  Definitely a step up from cheap Mexican... good full helpings, all entrees come with a tasty rice and beans, and they have a really nice assortment of maragaritas.  The free parking is also a really nice plus.  It's a little off the beaten path, but well worth a trip for a nice quiet meal, especially when the weather is nice as they have a nice outdoor patio.  Try the chorizo tacos... they're great!

This place is legit. I've ordered a whole bunch of times since I moved to this neighborhood and I've tried a lot of there menu and all of it has been good. If you are looking for the Americanized Cantonese we all grew up with, done right, order from here. Just have cash ready.

After reading LaBan's Chinatown restaurant run-down, Ting Wong struck me a the first establishment I needed to visit. A simple, inexpensive, low-décor, duck house--how could this not be first on the list?

My girlfriend and I visited on a Monday evening and left smiling. 

Upon entering we were greeted by our server and seated in one of the restaurant's small pick of tables. We shared the Duck Wonton Soup, Roast Pig, and Beef Chow Fun with Black Bean Sauce. All classic and delicious.

The Roast Pig, in particular, was the pick of the lot. Succulent, boneless pork surrounded by a skin crispier and more flavorful than a plate of cracklins. 

Their menu is expansive but Ting Wong seems to do soup, duck, and pork the best. A simple glance at their front-of-house kitchen (lined with roast ducks, pork belly, vats of meat broth, ribs, and more) quickly confirms this hypothesis. 

One interestin

The employees here were extremely polite and the service was great compared to other fast food restaurants. The manager and staffs came by to ask "How's everything?" several times by the guests table. For me this is rarity in fast food chain restaurants.

I had an extremely sad experience due to the behaviours of the staff. The team wasn't paying attention to the customers , were busy with their own talks and careless. The place was empty, was seated at the bar also was told to try couple of drinks which I didn't like so I politely refused. Later they told me so casually that my computer has an issue so it don't take ur order to kitchen . The male guy told the waitress in front of me to ask me n offer me some drink n "Just asked her whatever she wants" then waitress comes to me says casually i forgot to ring in ur order can we give u some drink. I told them i don't want any drink and then the male guy told me rudely that she is being "courteous" Really ? and then he was extremely rude and called me some unnecessary and not required lines suggesting that it's my fault instead. I had to walk out of the restaurant.

Ha.  Never thought I'd write a review for airport food, but here it is.  Philly's airport is in the last part (as far as I can tell) of a major rebuild.  Part of this change is an increase in a few higher end restaurants.  One of these is Sky Asian Bistro.

Walking in is a little difficult due to the masses of people trying to get to their gate and the amount of tables they squeezed into this place.  We found a cubby-hole in the corner.  We received our menus quickly and she quickly followed up with our drinks.  They have the usual assortment of sushi but the prices were a little high (expected as it's an airport).  California rolls were $4.50, but any kind of real fish was $6.50+ per roll.  My wife got the Cali rolls and she liked them ok, nothing earth shattering.  I got the Tuna Rolls and was impressed by the quantity and quality of the tuna.  They did a great job.

Disorganized staffing and seating and highly prejudiced. If I could give them zero, then I would. The staff/management do not treat you respectively and often snap at you just because they want to. My sister was standing near the bar because there was no room and a server wanted to get by and the server screeched "EXCUSE ME" at her. 

There was a family there who were being completely disrespectful toward us and sent an 8 year old child to tell us to quiet down in a public space (literally it's a restaurant and bar). We weren't being any louder than any other table as everyone was speaking loudly in the establishment. Every other table had people talking, drinking and enjoying a good time but they chose a table of Asian people to come tell us to quiet down. Management completely failed at being unbiased and poorly handled the situation.
The staff was very disrespectful. The guy ringing us up gave us a lot of attitude when we were ordering. We asked for straws since there wasn't any and he just looked at us and walked away.

I've tried time and time again with this restaurant. In the past I've left before even ordering but I decided to give them another chance. The entire staff was stressed and uncomfortable and fed that energy to their customers. Our waitress was trying very hard and you could tell it was out of her control, which goes to show that the upper management is the reason behind slow and rude service. This time I went there were employees screaming in the kitchen, customers (myself included) waiting upwards of 40 minutes for simple dishes, and lower level staff taking the brute for these actions. 
Every time I've been here it has been the managers that cause the chaos and discord and it really takes a toll on their employees and customers. 
Certainly my last attempt at eating here.

Staff was rude and inconsiderate to travelers stuck overnight due to bad weather who were resting at the gate next to their restaurant. Additionally, I watched one of the staff members drop a bin of clean silverware and then proceed to put it back in the clean bin and use it for customers. Absolutely disgusting.

The restaurant is very nice and food was great!  My only issue is with hostess staff... Extremely unfriendly, and acted as they were doing me a favor to speak with me or deal with me in anyway... This is the first impression for your restaurant and certainly not a good one.  Please address it!!

The newest market stall in the Reading Terminal Market is called Fox and Son.  This is one of the most attractive stalls in the entire market with its striped canopy awning as if it were at a carnival.  Well the food will take you to that carnival.  You see there are corn cogs, funnel cakes, fried cheese curds - you get the picture.  Even trendy poutine is here.  I'm not a huge fan of corn dogs but since they are the specialty here, I tried one again.  I also ordered chimichurri sauce to go with it.  The corn dog was okay - I guess I need to have a spicier hot dog inside to balance out the corn bread but the chimmichurri sauce to put on it was excellent.  Still keep in mind you're def paying more than what you would at a carnival for the corn dog and sauce but I'm sure rents at the Reading Terminal Market aren't cheap.

I heard their food was good but when our group tried to seat ourselves, the waitress came over and became very hostile. We explained that we had been ignored so we had to seat ourselves. Needless to say, we told her that her services weren't necessary. Worst service ever. This restaurant needs better management and waitresses that understand customer service (even at the most fundamental level).

DO NOT EAT HERE. TERRIBLE STAFF. 
I cannot rate the food because they never took my order.
The rudest staff  I have ever seen. The server would not give you more than 10 seconds to look at the menu and would leave the table if you do and then make you wait for 15 mins before she comes around to ask rudely "Are you ready?".
The Manager when notified was even more rude. He said the staff is just to busy to wait and you have to make up your mind soon or you can find another place.

I love getting to eat delicious vegan food and being able to support a business that cares for its employees and the community at large. The food is always consistently solid vegan comfort food...I generally go for the scrambles, tots, and a side of the sausage (mushroom) patty. So good. I understand it may not be everyones preference, but it is my go to place for breakfast and lunch in the city. I understand why they are not open for dinner, but if it was I would regularly get dinner also.

I don't understand the comments about being overpriced or the attitude of the staff. Their business model is to make sure they can pay their staff a living wage while not decreasing the quality of the food, especially during Covid, and I am more than happy to be a part of that as a customer.

I've "dined" at this "restaurant" a few times.  The first time was exciting bc I was so anxious to try the soup dumplings...and they were good...so I explained away the rude, abrupt, inhospitable staff bc it was very busy.  The next time, I came for lunch, it wasn't nearly as busy and the waitstaff was just as rude, making us feel unwelcome and rushed.  For some reason we came again, and once again (surprise surprise), the entire staff seemed annoyed to have customers, mad if you don't want to share a table with strangers, no pleasantries, barely acknowledge you, until you look like you are finishing your meal and they just can't wait to give you a bill and take your plates (literally, as I was picking up my last bite).  Rudely and loudly gave us some bullsh*t line that it's $15 to drink your own beer/wine bc they serve now...since when... girl lied and said a year.
Food is decent.

VERY IMPOLITE STAFF!! 
Heard so much about this place so just had to try it out. The servers and waitresses are actually very rude. They had this unpleasant face as we even walked through the door. The moment we sat down, they came to us for taking our order. 
On asking questions about the dishes, the waitresses (2 of them came together like siamese twins) started making annoyed faces & rolling their eyes while answering our questions. They didn't even answer our questions properly leaving us to still guess what we were ordering. There was no courtesy at all.
We were looking for a chicken dish which was more dry . They could not recommend one. Instead were just pointing at the pictures around the menu and mumbling something in English. SO UNHELPFUL. Their vibe was "how dare you ask me"

The food we somehow chose arrived quickly. They were delicious!

This place is terrible. The staff are rude and either don't talk to you at all and keep you waiting for 10 minutes just standing there, or they tell you that you need to be more patient with them when they finally bother to acknowledge you. I was told over the phone the order would be done in 20 minutes, and I arrived in 30. The order took an additional 20 minutes to complete with me just standing there not being addressed because they didn't even start it until I walked in. They were not busy. I was the only patron in the establishment. I brought it to the manager's attention politely and asked how much longer it would be and he pointed to the griddle, glared at me and said "we're a little bit busy, okay? You think you can forgive us? We're making it now." As I stood there waiting in those 20 minutes I was never told how long it would be from that point, or asked if I needed anything.

Food is always good, but when I went there last weekend we experienced poor customer service. We waiting 20 mins before we received our drinks from the  bar. We watched the bald head bartender have side conversations instead of making our drinks. We kept asking our server to check on them and all she said was they were being worked on. Communication and Customer Service was horrible that night!!!! No apologies nothing.

I had dinner at Vedge recently and was extremely disappointed with my experience.  The host who greeted us at the door was shockingly rude. He had such a pompous attitude, and for lack of better words, treated us like garbage when we arrived fifteen minutes late. When we were seated instead of being wished a good meal, we were reminded of what time we had to leave. I was shocked that such a reputable restaurant would elect to have such a rude individual be the first person to greet your guests.

Upon being seated we couldn't help but notice the cluster of staff hovered in one spot. They were also quite loud, and I was actually appalled at some of the profanities I could hear clear as day from where I was seated. The gatherings of staff happened frequently throughout the evening and it seemed as though they were all much more interested in socializing than working.

The food is phenomenal, wait staff is great. The owner not so great. He is ridiculously rude to his staff (only to the women that I've ever witnessed) My family and I ate there tonight and witnessed him yell across the restaurant to a waitress to stop talking to her table. She was so embarrassed. He told her she talks too much. The table she was talking to actually was asking her a question- we sat next to them so we heard. I felt sorry for her. This isn't the first time we felt he was ignorant to his staff. If it wasn't for a couple of our favorite waitress's we would NOT go back. It's not just the food that matters it's the people too.

The staff was very rude. My friends and I came in and I told the hostess we were going to just get drinks and she was rude and just pointed to the bar. Then, we wanted to sit at a table and a woman with short & dyed hair SCREAMED 'R U EATING FOOD THIS IS ONLY FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE DINING IN' They all seemed like miserable people.

My friends and I were excited to try this place and everything about it was just not it. The staff was honestly really rude with the exception of the upstairs hostess and the food runner with glasses. 

We waited at the bar downstairs until we were let upstairs, and the female bartender wouldn't ring up our margs separately even though no tab had been created, she just didn't feel like clicking two extra buttons on her literal hand held tablet. We asked to have a full rim of salt instead of half and they said no. We asked to send back a drink that tasted really off and they said "idk if we are allowed to waste it." 

Don't expect regular restaurant service, you order on your phone and it's really difficult to get the attention of staff.

Food was fine but everyone there needed a vibe check.

One of the rudest people to answer the phone in a long time. As soon as the lady answered, she was incredibly rude and then when I was done ordering, she hung up on me without even telling me how long till my food was ready. I called back to ask how long and she responded "3 minutes" with an attitude and hung up. 

They are lucky that the food is good because their staff is frankly terrible.
Horrible service. Our waitress was nonexistent. The support staff tried to fill in. Our food was also cold.

This particular restaurant has consistently demonstrated abysmal customer service. The owner must be making a ton of money on their other ventures and not care for this one because I can tell the staff here is making him/her lose $$$ by the minute. Can you guys believe I went there about a month ago and there was an hour wait? An hour. Even though the place was damn near empty. Smh

AWFUL service each and every time we have given them the chance. Just left there after sitting at the normal seat yourself bar tops. Only after asking would be be able to receive help (and them saying "sure") did the rude bartender curtly let us know that those weren't serviced during lunch. Managers galore, yet no one friendly nor did they care enough to serve us. We immediately exited and happily settled for Wendy's next door!

Food was great and worth the wait... but the staff is horrible! The ladies helping in the front are rude, pushy, and obnoxious. There were many times I was asking questions and was either met with a smart ass remark or just plain ignored. I will not be coming back again.

Depending on the staff you get, your experience can be wildly different.  There are a couple of guys that have been in good spirits each time I've been there, but a weekend younger female barista and the female owner/manager are awful on the regular.  Snarky, disparaging comments, condescending attitudes in response to simple questions.  They seem to have missed the memo that they are in the food service industry and part of that is being professional and courteous.  

The first time we were there, we sat down after they showed us our table.  Then we got attitude that we're supposed to order and pay at the counter before sitting down.  Uh, ok.  Duh, stupid customers.

Another time, my father got the ice when he asked if he could add toast to his brunch.  Uh, ok. Whatever. Weird but not a deal-ender.

Incredible place for brunch!! The bloody mary is phenomenal. It is smooth, not watery, but not chunky as hell. Nothing drives me more insane than swallowing chunks of horseradish through my straw. This makes me want to gag, and it certainly doesn't make me want to order another round. But, alas, that was not a problem at Mixto. The drink came garnished with olives, celery, lime, and lemon. Pick your poison, AND, my favorite part of the drink were the scallions in the mix. Simply delicious. 

The food is also mouth-watering-amazingness (one word). I'm an eggs benedict girl, but I could not deny myself some delicious Cuban fare. So I ordered the Gallo Pinto and my friend ordered the Argentinian steak and eggs. Everything was cooked to perfection! 

Just as a side note, and something I really appreciate, is when a waitress asks if you are finished with your cocktail.

Was there recently after church and found the staff surly, dismissive and without any hint of basic kindness or genuine concern for the customer.   It was exactly as if we we're inconveniencing them.   Very disappointed and frankly annoyed.    Will never go back.   Should I even begin to describe the "waffle"?
Food was bland and completely uninspired. The real disappointment was the terrible customer service and rude wait staff. No wonder the place was crowded.

The food was subpar (and chicken undercooked), but it was the horrible service that stood out in my mind. "Sorry!," could be heard coming out of a waiter's mouth every five seconds.

I walked in and was greeted by three hostesses. One took me to a booth, sat me down, and them mumbled something that sounded like, "I'll be back with two waters." She came back a few minutes later with only silverware in hand, and I asked her if she could also bring a coffee with the waters. She laughed at me and said, "I'm not your waiter!," to which I replied with a scowl. She then seemed flustered and told me, "It is going to be a while, we are really busy." This is not how you treat a customer! I don't care if you are not my waiter, you can still get a drink order for me, especially when there are two other hostesses and "it is going to be a while." Rude!

I have eaten at this place at least a couple times, going back as an attempt to give it another shot, and another and another, because I don't like to give a bad review based on just one experience. I've worked in the restaurant business for a couple of years and I know that every restaurant can have an "off" day, but this place is just always terrible unfortunately. 

The food is really quite gross...the most recent time I went there was with a pretty big group and everyone's food was messed up that I was with. My friend's salad had a toothpick in it. My sausage had a piece of metal in it. My friend's burger was meant to be medium came out way past well and was bordering being burnt to a crisp. The bun it came on was literally as hard as a hockey puck, it was like they were just using up old buns from several days before. 

Besides the food, the service wasn't great either.

Food is great, but customer service was HORRENDOUS. The waitress had an attitude and seemed as if he didn't want to be there. He threw the drink and and they don't want you to know that the tip is included just so they'll get more money. They never checked up on us to see if even we needed anything. We could understand it was a busy day, but customers are priority and the service is a must have.

Staff is very rude and unprofessional.they are always cursing on front of staff and playing. Also they tend to get orders wrong alot I had to go up to the counter  3 times until they got my order right.sometimes food is cold.

I have been to this restaurant before but I went today and had an awful experience.  We arrived by 1215 pm for lunch and had to order quickly because of limited time.  The restaurant was relatively empty. We received our drinks and appetizers on time but waited, as others who arrived after us not only ordered food but received their food.  As of 1259pm ( when i left the restaurant - we had not received our food.  The waiter was no help as he failed to enter our order in the the system until 1244.  When we asked for the manager, the waiter was not helpful in getting him to us and we finally had to summon a server support person ( busboy)to get the manager.  We we complained about the service and demanded our food be provided to us for take away ( since our lunch time window had expired ). We also asked the manager the we be provided the food without cost .

As Pitruco's first paying customer (ever!) I feel obligated to write a review of their pizza. I tried the Neopolitan and was so amazed by the pizza that I had to take a picture of it. The crust was thin, a bit crisp and charred in spots. All of the ingredients were top notch including the tasty mozzarella, sweet tomato sauce, and fresh basil. And it was fast....my pizza was prepared from scratch and done in five minutes or less. What is so amazing (or odd?) is that this ranks as the best pie in town IMO, a little better than what they serve up at Zavino...and from a truck! So good in fact that I had to pick up a box somewhere else to take another pie home. They have other pizzas too featuring gourmet toppings like sopressata but none top out at more than $9 or so. They also have sodas and liters of San Pelligrino.

The cheesesteaks were okay. The service, however, is another story...
The staff were unfriendly,  rude, and completely unhelpful.
I received looks of disgust from the girl taking orders just for asking a question, when ordering my food. When I asked for assistance at their soda machine, which was out of tea, rootbeer, and cherry coke, she sighed heavily and without acknowledging me went into the back room. Was she helping me or not???

The food is very good and the ambiance is wonderful. The service is SO slow no matter if it is full or empty. Additionally, most of the staff are quite rude and do not seem to care. I have given this place 5 tries and cannot say that I have ever been happy when leaving. Which is sad because I work upstairs - would love to make this a go to spot but I can't justify it for happy hour, lunch or dinner. 

Some examples: an hour and a half for lunch, asked to wait outside for our dessert because they needed the table. 20 minutes for two glasses of wine at happy hour. Server rolled his eyes at a guest who preferred oil and vinegar on their salad. They have no food between 3-5. Always takes more than 10 minutes to get your credit card back after handing it over to pay your check.

The food was very good but the service was absolutely terrible.  One woman was serving the whole room.  She was working hard but all over the place.  There was a gentleman standing by the kitchen who would fill get glasses of water ready for her and bring food from the kitchen to a station for her but he never served any food to the tables.  I don't understand why they have a guy just standing there 75% of the time while customers are sitting there looking at their food, and waiting forever to get it.

thought we would get a warm drink.  We popped in and were immediately treated like second class citizens.  I wanted a table they forced us to sit at the bar.  I decided to order breakfast potatoes and sausage in addition to my hot chocolate an my friend's tea.  The server girl took a long time to bring the tea and she spilled my hot chocolate.  She was very nervous, she brought out the potatoes a long time before we got the sausage.  It was terrible service and timing.  Many minutes later a young man came to our rescue and brought us more potatoes and finally we got the sausage.  He was good and tried to make up for the terrible service of the young girl. We should have been given our food and drink at no charge for what we endured.

Expect poor service.  Each time I've been here something has gone wrong and it's all because of the lackluster effort of the staff.  This morning, the woman working the registered mumbled something at me when I stepped up and when I said "sorry, didn't catch that" she simply rolled her hand at me in a "just order" kind of way.  There was no line, the phone wasn't ringing, there were other staff working... she clearly wasn't slammed - or even busy - no excuse to be rude.  So whatever, I placed my order and waited.  And waited.  And waited.  Until I eventually asked about my order - which had been placed aside as a call-in order.  No apology for having me wait 20 minutes, no indication what-so-ever that a mistake was made, not even a mumble this time... just an uncaring hand extending what turned out to be a now cold breakfast sandwich.

Awful service. The food is great, but I had a horrible experience with customer service. I have been to this restaurant multiple times and enjoyed the food, but when I ordered take out it took more than 2 hours for our food to show up. When we called to check on the order after an hour, they told us the food was on its way. However, it still did not arrive an hour later. When we asked to speak with a manager, the manager was rude and non-apologetic about their mistake. It took them more than 15 minutes on the phone to finally apologize for the mistake. It's a shame when a restaurant with such great food has such poor service.
Poor service. The waiter would not even answer you when there were only 3 customers in the restaurant. waited 20 minutes for the check.

Incredibly rude staff. I know it's a fast food burger joint and I'm not walking in expecting to be treated like I'm at a Steven Starr restaurant, but these people treat you terribly. A little kindness and respect goes a long long way in this world.

TERRIBLE service.  Came in and sat down at the bar, right in front of the kitchen doors.  There was TONS of staff, standing behind the counter there, walking in and out of the kitchen.  I was there a WHILE with menus in hand.  Nobody even looked at me let alone greeted me.  Left hungry and annoyed.  How hard would "hi" be?  Wont be returning.  Pretentious and tbh I dont love their beer anyway.

This place is #1 in both terrible service and utter rudeness. Our goal was simply to order food at the host station and take it to go. The entire process, 1/2 of which was time spent trying to get someone to recognize us, took 50 minutes. The restaurant was not busy (only 5 tables occupied) and it appeared at times as though the staff was intentionally trying to ignore us and most of the other customers that were waiting. The Asian customers were getting attention and being treated with respect while all but one of our group and others waiting at the host station were black. It felt racial, especially when the arrogant employee finally took our order. He had an attitude and clearly didn't want to help us. He reluctantly took our order and after another ~25" we were on our way. Not cool.

the wait was soo long, and we were getting angry as the waitstaff walked passed and didnt stop and help us for a long time. 

Once we finally got a server, we ordered right away since we had to wait so long just to get a server to come and help us. So we placed our order, and we literally waited 45 minutes to receive our meals. This service here is a joke! I dont even think a manager was on duty at this shit show. I understand you are busy, but they always seem to be and should prepare on how they will assist each table in a timely manner. 

When the food finally came out it was tasty, but waiting for refills was terribly long, asking for napkins, sauces for our nuggets came way later after we had already eaten most of our meals. 

The food is always on point, but I cant get past the terrible service, so I wont be back here again.

After we had been cleared by the ever attentive bus boys, our sever came and offered dessert and dropped the check. 10 minutes later, we were still waiting for him to pick up the payment. Another server came by and picked it up to run our credit card. Shortly after, our server came over to ask if he had brought us our bill! Unreal!

This has been a disappointing and disheartening experience. This was the absolute WORST service we have ever experienced. It was almost surreal, an out of body expletive watching the train wreck of what passed for service in this place. Over seasoned, unbalanced, salty food is FORGIVABLE, but inattentive, absentminded service is INEXCUSABLE. Waiting 20 minutes with nothing but water and menus at the outset of the meal sets a pretty poor tone. Making customers wait to pay at the end of their meal is completely UNACCEPTABLE !

This goes to the poor service. We had issues throughout our meal that were inexcusable. We had to ask several times for an appetizer, then 1 main course came after everyone's meal and one of the kids beer received ice cream even though the table was served. Even getting and paying the check was a challenge.  We had 2 waiters and neither seemed attentive to our table or cared that things were slow and wrong. Seems like many others have the same experience. 

Go to KOP - much better!

Sadly the food was very good

Rude and snarky staff from hostess to wait staff. Unaccomidating.

Food- rushed, assembly line, in-and out atmosphere.

Not worth the poor service.

I think one or two waitresses eventually felt how upset I was but none did try to simply refill my empty glass of water and apologize for this poor service!! Perhaps waiters/waitress rotate for these tables every 30 minutes so there is absolutely no consistency, but this is UNACCEPTABLE. Prices are not lower at these tables!

I saw much more attentive waiters / waitresses for patrons seated at regular dinner room tables, on the other side (but none cared about me, my sad thirsty and dehydrated look and empty glasses, nor did the pseudo-maitres d'hotel always walking around but not looking for patrons' satisfaction). UNACCEPTABLE

Cool location, lots of room. Friendly staff. Slow service at the register. No table service. Waited in line for skillet for 10 minutes only to be told that the kitchen closed 10 minutes early and wouldn't make them. So hungry, so pissed. Won't be back any time soon.

The food was good but the service was terrible. Once we were seated, the server brought water and tea right away but from then on, we only saw the server once more when he took our order (which took twenty minutes). We didn't have our drinks refilled and no one came to check on us to even ask how the food was. Come for the food but don't expect great service

We have been customers at Mulherin's since day 1, literally. We had always touted it as our favorite restaurant in the neighborhood and dined there at least once a week. Unfortunately, we have noted a significant and steady decline in service. 

Sitting at the bar USED to be a pleasure and was our "go-to" spot. The bar tenders were attentive, polite, and knowledgable. On MULTIPLE occasions now, after being escorted to the bar by the hostess, the bar tender just looked at us and said, rudely, "have you checked in with the hostess??" I understand that it isn't open seating and they need to confirm that the patron was, indeed, given the spot by the hostess, but I would just prefer that they maybe start with a "good evening." This may seem nit picky, but I expect employees to be polite at a nice restaurant.

We have also noted downright poor service by the servers, too.

Went here last night with my boyfriend. Their food and mixed drink options are quite excellent. The only negative thing last night, was that our waiter was pretty bad. Nice enough guy, but extremely inattentive. Never once asked us how our food was, etc. The waitress that brought our entrées out was more attentive. 

They just need some tweaking with their service, and they'd be perfect.

Terrible service. Owner called my party liars due to a miscommunication between the kitchen and our waitress. Waiting staff is not attentive whatsoever and runs around like a chicken with no head, running around with no clue as to what's going on. Owner ruined experience. Never going back there again. This will probably be the only review I will ever leave on Yelp. I made my account about 5 minutes ago, that's how terrible the service was.

Totally over rated. Very, very poor service. The portions are small for the money. Our waiter never ever came back to our table after dropping off our food to insure things were ok, which they were not. We could not order another drink. There are a large number of hosts and hostesses circulating ostensibly to insure great service. We flagged down one of the hosts to get more flat bread for our hummus and he never brought it back. We got a 3rd waiter involved and he finally brought us more bread after over 30 minutes of waiting. By that time all of our food was cold. Our bill was incorrect on top of everything.

A place to see and be seen, but not for reasonable service or remarkable food for the money.

Pros: 

- Friendly staff 
- conveniently located near Morgan's Pier in case you want to go out and have a bit of fun after you eat. 
- pretty decent selection of games.  

Cons: 
- incredibly slow service 
- the waitress wasn't customer service oriented at all.

After a long ride from the Northeast, I was starving.  After we were seated we started looking at the menus.  After 10-15 minutes the waitress came over and informed us they were the wrong menus.  We finally got water and coffee, without enough creamers so we had to wait again. I decided what I would order and was informed the waffle maker was broken so I couldn't have that.  Is there only one waffle maker in the whole place? I picked pancakes instead.  They were fine, not worth the drive of one hour or all the waiting we had to do.  My meal came a good 5 minutes after everyone else's, which was a bit annoying.  The waitress was not attentive at all.  We had to wave her down if we wanted extra creamers, ketchup, etc.  I definitely won't drive there again.  The others in my party liked their meal, I think, but with the poor service

1. The wait was terrible. We came in for a quick bite before going to a concert two blocks down. The drinks came out timely but the cheesesteak and fries came out over 45 minutes after that. I finished my whole root beer float before receiving a bite to eat. The only plus was that we got seated relatively quickly before spending way more time (almost 2 hours) here than we thought we would. 

2. Customer service was terrible. The waitress who gave us our drinks threw my spoon for my float on the dirty menu that was on the table. The other waitress who took our orders wasn't friendly nor attentive. At one point we were looking for her for some water and she was actually just outside the window chilling and drinking a soda. I noticed that she did a poor job checking up on others in her section too.

3. When we finally got the food, the cheesesteak was so so SO disappointing.

It is a great place, and the staff is extremely patient despite the locals that were extremely rude while we were there.  They are "servers", not "servants", you know what I mean?  As an artist myself, I was a little ashamed of the self important jerks as they talked about how important they were loud enough that all could hear and all but knocked two patrons out of their seat to take up more room in the restaurant.  That being said, the food was great, my drink was fine, and the server was attentive despite the snaps in the air beside us to get her attention.  Grace under pressure is an underrated talent, and the full staff there should be commended for that talent.

As always terrific food and highly attentive service. My fourth visit and all expectations continue to be met. But I'd like to mention the exceptionally high level of professionalism of the staff. They handled a difficult situation with a large, rowdy group that was disrupting the dining experience of others with grace. They quickly acknowledged the distribution, tried to quiet the group (who were truly loud and foul-mouthed) and then moved us to a different room. It was a Saturday night so I'm sure they were completely booked but they did not put up any resistance to the requests from several different tables to be moved away from the obnoxious, selfish, inconsiderate group.  It was not Mulherin's fault the group was loud and offensive- they were certainly place in a difficult position - but I really appreciate how they handled it.

The WORST place I have been to in a very longtime. 
Lets start with the rude Hostess....how about you greet customers or at least be helpful when they ask you a question.
The Bartender....another rude character who said less than 10 words to me the entire time I was there.
But why did I have to sit at the bar for 8 minutes before someone came to greet me or ask me for my order? Oh wait, you would have to give me a menu first and that didn't happen either.
Somehow though...the two Caucasian women to my left that came in after me not only were greeted but given excellent service. The Caucasian man that came in that sat to my right was given exceptional service as well. Hmmmm.....is this a trend? I would say so.
What did I not look "rich" enough? or my skin was too dark?
Then....I get my food..fries burnt to the max...did I get any assistance from the bartender?

The wait staff was friendly when they came around, but they weren't super attentive.

Definitely enjoyed my meal, but the service was so-so.  I know it was busy that day but it put me off a little.  Check it out!  The food was fantastic!

We had dined in your restaurant yesterday afternoon from about 2-5pm. When we arrived there was only about 6 tables and a handful of people at the bar. My group had about 6 adults and 4 children. Our server Devon was not very helpful from the time we sat down. We ordered fries and cheesesteaks (the 4$ cheese steak which did not specify it was a half) and the order came out wrong with two people not getting their food bc of the lack of detail on ordering. She was not very attentive to our table at all, we were seated at the two larger tables in the back. We realized she was under staffed and tried to take that into consideration while eating and drinking, however she never once asked our table if we were ok or needed anything else. Instead I felt like I was bothering her every time I had to stop her to ask for food or drinks.

Everything was great apart from SUPER unfriendly staff at the door - B and Tina were their names i believe. Shame to see other people have said the same thing and nothing has been done to change it. Your front of house staff are the first people your customers see so should be a better representation of what's on the inside! Everyone else was lovely and very attentive!

We were able to watch everything coming in and out of the kitchen on the one side, and the butchers slicing up pigs on the other. While it is certainly not a good spot for the faint of heart, I thought it really added to the experience. We couldn't stop taking pictures! 

The staff there was all on top of their game, knowledgeable, friendly, and attentive. Although we had one main server, everyone attended to our needs. If someone noticed we needed more water, for example, they came over to fill it. Unlike many places that have that sort of collaborative serving, we didn't feel overwhelmed by waiters and waitresses constantly bothering us, nor did we feel as if our waitress was not taking care of us. Like I said, it was clear that we had our server, and everyone else was just there to provide a helping hand. 

The food, although not great, was very good.

Let me preface this review by saying all the food was absolutely incredible. We were a party of 6 and the appetizer, entrees, and desserts were all fantastic. The atmosphere is noisy and slightly cramped but it makes the experience intimate and is nothing to complain about. That being said, our meal started off fine... We are college friends who only get to see each other once a year so we were expecting a relaxing meal with lots of our BYOB wine. We started to feel rushed when all 6 of our entrees were brought out within a minute of us taking the last bite of our appetizer. The waiter was nice and attentive but clearly he wanted us to finish. Having been a waitress for 6 years I was confused because all though the small area is crowded, there was no one waiting at the door to be seated.
Also, the staff was so attentive and friendly, they truly elevated the whole experience. I can't say enough good things, we left so full and satisfied and just HAPPY about the whole evening.

Have been a handful of times. The food and drinks never disappoint! But when it comes to the service.. its very spotty. I can say that i only had one great service experience here, the majority of the time it was a bit sad. For instance some of the servers were completely unknowledgeable of the food and spirits they have listed. Also have had instances where we felt forgotten as the servers never returned for very long periods of time. We also felt as we were a burden because it was late at night and they kept switching servers because it was towards kitchen closing time, and they just kept disappearing for extended periods visibly doing side work and acting as if we were a bother. Not to mention they have forgotten items we have ordered, but the most entertaining experience with a server is when he crumbed our table with the drink menu! Keepin it classy..
What we got instead was a not-so-amazing-but-decent meal with attentive, professional, friendly staff.

Adorable decor, friendly and attentive staff, with great service! All the food we ordered was delicious and came out in a timely manner. Presentation of all food and drink was great! It was an overall great dinning experience!
Plates were a bit small & it's a little pricey but worth it!

Eating here is reminiscent of the elegant dining this restaurant must have offered a 100 years ago. The atmosphere is stunningly beautiful, food was delicious and the wait staff friendly, professional and attentive. My only complaint was that they were too attentive. At the time we ate, there were more waiters than tables and they stood lined up just a few yards away from our table, watching and waiting. It felt a little unnerving. All in all, though, a very good meal.

Wouldn't normally review a place while it was still so new,but the complete lack of attention to service was kind of astounding.  Went on Sunday night of Labor Day weekend. Not packed by any means,but the slowest least attentive service we have ever had. Restaurant is beautiful, great attention to detail.  Bartender seemed attentive and on point
 We have told neighbors to just go for drinks at this point. Appetizer came out after entrees. Food was good,but not remarkable. Total process for 2 quesadillas,1 shared entree and 2 beers was over 2 hours. When check came  there were 3 items that we had not ordered adding at least 15 minutes to the evening. At NO point did anyone ask how our food was,did we need anything,etc. Seemed thoroughly untrained despite a professional restaurant owner. Will give them another chance because the concept and visual execution are so beautiful.

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday and service was below par for an upper-end steakhouse. My water was not kept at least half full and at one point I had to drink from his glass as we dined on somewhat salty steaks. There were waiters in blue shirts near our table who avoided me flagging them down when we needed water or new napkins. They were busy chatting with each other. Only until the floor manager came out to survey and makes his rounds did the staff look more active and attentive. The food coming out the kitchen was timely and mostly tasty - especially the appetizers. The tuna tartare was on point. I did not like that the floor waiters were being attentive and chatty to certain tables throughout the night when we happened to order a large amount of food.

I have been to this place many times, as of late it has been a hit or miss.

The place is nice, friendly. Open to anyone who is a paying customer. The service is only alright, the watering staff is very attentive and will refill your water/drink almost immediately, however the wait staff is not as attentive. Or they just stand there and watch you eat; a very uncomfortable feeling.

During one experience, the food was great! Everything was fresh and was cooked well. Another time I went I got the Mee Siam, the food wasn't seasoned as well as it could be. During my most recent experience I got the pad thai, and the noodles were uncooked. I told the wait staff, and they didn't understand, I had 4 people come to me before someone understood that it wasn't cooked and not that it was cold. They apologized and of course got me a new one but this time they overcooked it.

Wonderful food, lovely atmosphere, attentive waitstaff! Couldn't ask for a better experience. 

Although we arrived at the dandelion between meal times, it was very full. The staff was still very attentive to our needs, even though they were extremely busy. The food was served in a timely manner and presented in a beautiful manner. 

By only complaint was that I ordered a ginger beer and was given lemonade instead and the waiter sill charged me for the beverage. Other than that slight mishap, everything was great!

Definitely recommend!

I ordered a fiesta cheesesteak and took it to Wissahickon Brewing Company.  The fiesta Cheesesteak lived up to its name, there was a party going on in that roll.  The fiesta cheesesteak had fried onions, mushrooms, green peppers, pepperoni and sauce.  Was it a party in that roll or a train wreck?  The only flavor that really stood out was of a canned mushroom. In my humble opinion, when you have that much stuff together it needs to spend time on the grill together cooking and blending and mixing flavor so you have some kind of uniform taste.  The good news is it was big and we were at Wissahickon Brewing Company.  I had at least two beers and they were all (maybe had more than 2) very flavorful and good.

Came here for brunch - loved the shakshuka and cheese curds! I got one of the pouch drinks which I wasn't crazy about but it's fun and worth getting it. The mimosa was good too. I came in the winter in one of their outdoor booths, I really wish it was a little more spacious and kept more warm (it was freezing.) I'd be back in warmer weather or if I were able to get an indoor reservation!

OVERRATED!! It was expensive and not even that good. Dinner for two of us was $200 and we ordered one drink each and no dessert. Speaking of dessert, the options were meh. We ended up going somewhere else to get dessert that night. We ordered about 5 plates and ended up really liking only one of them. It absolutely wasn't worth the high price tag. Save your money and go somewhere else.

The food was ok, not great not bad. The service was fine. The prices are far too high for what you get. At least one of three things needs to change: the prices (down) , the food quality (up to amazing), or the quantity of food for the price (portions are small). Right now the price/quantity mix is just out of whack.
I thought this was kind of overrated.  Food was alright but I thought that it was not worth the price

Every detail shines through here, from the classically and beautifully styled rooms, tables and bars to a simple brunch meal. The beer list is well curated and the fact you can get a 20oz pour of your top choice ( I went with the Prima Pils) adds a little extra joy. 

A great place for dinner with the parents or to celebrate a special occasion, or even just because sometimes you want a big beer and a classic English breakfast. 

I chose a sausage egg and cheese with triple fried chips. Not health food by any means but so good you'll happily loosen your belt. The bread is buttery and a little crispy, with great flavor in the meat and satisfying texture from the gooey cheese and an egg that runs ever so slightly. The fries were thick, but crispy and we'll seasoned. Dessert and coffee satisfied, though I can't say it excelled. 

Staff and service are strong, cool without being aloof.

The service was pretty bad. They placed us towards the back when there were plenty of tables in the middle area where we would want to sit. They said they were 'reserved' but nobody sat in those tables the whole 2.5 hours we were there. So we were right next to the kitchen and bathrooms. Plus the table right behind us they placed a homeless woman there that spilled everything everywhere. It was horrible for the price we paid to eat there. The waitress took forever to give us the check after we said no to desserts. 

We're a minority so it makes me think that they were racist somehow and placed us all the way towards the back when there's clearly tables in the middle. 

All in all service was horrible, food was a little too pricey for the service they gave us and sitting us next to a homeless lady with all her bags.
Excellent for the $$. Obviously not the best, but the prices are very very reasonable. The venue is small ~10 people and byob, which is perfect for intimate meal.

Food here is pretty good, not great. The hummus, falafel were standard, but flavorful.. Pita was thin, and could have been fresher/warmer. My mixed kofta kebab platter(beef & chicken)served over a bed of rice(asked for yellow, but got brown) was tasty and moist. Had a bit of onion-tomato gravy on it, and a nice creamy garlic sauce on the side.  They also have tahina, cucumber yogurt and spicy mint sauces which I would have liked to try, but cost extra. Did not care for the hot sauce, it had an odd off-putting flavor. The side salad sucked. My friend loved her NY chicken on rice, calling it "comfort food". 

The atmosphere is nice. When you walk in it looks like a pizza take out shop, but you are led into an adjoining room which is nicely decorated. A table full of hookahs come out later in the eve I suppose. The service was friendly and accommodating.

Expensive.  It was good, but it wasn't so amazing that it should have cost quite so much.  We split our meal and even our salad, so that made it very reasonable.  That made the meal MUCH, MUCH more enjoyable.  We will definitely come back.

Taste: 7/10
Price: 9.3/10

$9.99 for this lunch special (I got nachos on the left and Sopes on the right)

Food was aight. The free chips (top row) were good tbh they were a little thicker than normal chips and a little more cooked so they were all super crispy and addicting to eat; HOWEVER that green dipping sauce for the chips was like dipping it in water lol come on dont do em like that 

The NACHOS were on point the chips were all crispy still plus them beans and chorizo chunks and peppers and cheese was some mmm mmm mmmm i like me some loaded nachos that arent soggy well done there

I got a Sopes because i had no clue what it was. TBH this was my first time eating an avocado in my life LOL it was actually pretty good tbh idk about paying $2 for an avocado over getting like a donut but again id needa experiment more with them. The sopes itself was ehhhhhhhhhhhh.
Food is good. But for the price they charge the portions are small and not what I expected for the price taste wise.

I wanted to update my review, since my latest experience here blew me out of the water.  Everything from start to finish was perfect.  It helped that we got sat in the beautiful outdoor patio area by the garden with the strung lights - very romantic.

Our server was extremely knowledgeable about the wine and helped us pick what to get based on our personal preferences/food choices.  

As for food, last time I visited was in October and the menu has completely changed since then, which means it rotates seasonally and that's always a nice plus.

To start, we split the lamb skewers appetizer.  Adorable presentation and the meat was so juicy and flavorful, it practically fell off the skewers.  Spicy dipping sauce was dope.  Homemade warm bread and olive oil for the table is also still delicious.

I heard a lot of great things about this place and want to give it another try but we were pretty underwhelmed by our first visit. 

The double Margherita pizza was a very good start to the meal. We followed that with two pastas and the wood fired pork chop. 

The Ferratini al frutti di mare was everyone's least favorite, it was very heavy on the marjoram and tasted very floral which was an odd flavor combo with the seafood. The pastas are small portions and the four of us left half of it on the plate. The carbonara was ok, the pasta seemed a little undercooked and it wasn't very flavorful. 

The wood fired pork chop was very tender and tasted good, but the sides of green beans and spinach were kind of bland and didn't add anything to the dish. 

The service was great, our server was attentive and gave good recommendations on the amount of food to order.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon this place and decided to give it a try. In terms of food and service, it was great. I loved how afterwards I didn't feel that gross, full feeling. I felt like the meal was light, senseable, and overall healthy. 

My biggest issue with the meal however is the price. Just went for a simple lunch, ended up costing almost $50 dollars. These prices are a little ridiculous and they really need to consider reducing the price. Remember, Ramen Bar, you're in UNIVERSITY CITY catering to poor college students, NOT Rittenhouse Square!!

This place is way overpriced and definitely lacking in their portions sizes for the prices of their entrees. The step down dining, is something I like. It's a slightly dark place. The lighting from the small track lights above do just enough illumination. It reminds me of a reformed wine cellar. The booths are tall, yet you sit at ground level. All around you are those scientific artist renderings of various species of seafood. Be that as it may, I wasn't impressed. Where as with Lacroix, I was treated to something special. This was kind of normal, average. I digress. I really love their complementary biscuit, served with sweet butter cream. More please! For our appetizer we had the small order of Muscles in garlic butter juice. I love seafood and Muscles especially. There was enough for the both of us and it came with a nice size of (Sourdough?) garlic bread.
You get the point right? Good food over-priced. Great dining atmosphere, great service, a little too expensive though.
Portions weren't as big as I was expecting for the food was tasty. A little overpriced for that size of the plate.
It wasn't the worst food I've ever eaten but extremely overpriced.

The most overpriced and overrated restaurant in the city.
Food is uniformly mediocre.
Service is poor. A constantly changing cast of characters (servers is a  misnomer) showed they couldn't have cared less about us.
The noise level is overwhelming and conversation inhibiting.
The menu prices are far in excess in relation to the uniformly poor food served late
 Food which should have been served hot was repeatedly served warm at best.
Ingredients of dishes  were misrepresented  by bored waitpeople (i.e., malt is not vanilla).
No one working here cares about customers and a general lack of interest is constantly reinforced.
Don't bother climbing the steps to the dining room. Definitely go elsewhere (or stay home).
Overrated and way too expensive. If you want to show off how much money you can spend, this is a great place. If you're looking for value and taste, especially for vegetarians, look elsewhere.

This place WAS a complete dive with awesome & affordable food 12 years ago but now it's totally overpriced. It still looks the same as it did back then, the portions are huge, the food tastes good but not for the prices. My husband and I ate here yesterday and ordered chicken and oxtail entrees with 2 extra sides and no drinks. They didn't not have all the items listed on the menu and the bill was over $50! With those kind of prices you'd expect they at least  try to improve on the service and esthetics of the restaurant. I will not come back here.
The restaurant itself is chic, but not fancy and luxury. The food is like meh. Does NOT worth the price at all, and $$ is like the maximum you should charge

Food was good - not spectacular and the price was way too high.  
Great ambiance for a casual stop in but still not worth the price.

I was super excited to try this place! But honestly it is NOT worth the price. 

This place is ridiculously expensive for no reason. It's just salads and toppings. I did like that they had hot toppings but still toppings. I paid like $12 for this meal. The salad was ok.... I enjoyed the array of options but the employees weren't that friendly while making my food. 

The taste could've been more flavorful and the bread could've been moister. Ultimately, wasn't that thrilled.
Over priced, over hyped. Not like the food was bad, but totally not worth the price. Don't mind paying more for food you could get much better going elsewhere? - this place might be for you.

Most of the food items were very good, but some of them were very average and just not worth the price. If money is not an issue, this is a good place to try. Otherwise, make sure you stick to a few great menu items or you will be disappointed. I'll start with the items I thought were very good. I really enjoyed the Albondigas (Lamb Meatballs,Shaved Manchego), Ensalda de Jamon (Serrano Ham & Fig Salad,
Cabrales, Spiced Almonds), Alcachofas y Setas (Artichokes,
Wild Mushrooms, Black Truffles Manchego Flatbread) Gambas al Ajillo
(Garlic Shrimp), and Alcachofas a la Parmesana
(Parmesan Artichokes), The Manchego Pasamontes
(Truffled Lavender Honey) was unique, but the portion was very small.  The Patatas Bravas (Spicy Potatoes) were bland. The Chorizo was very chewy, and all I tasted was salt. The Scallops were average at best, and you get two scallops cut in half (so four pieces) for $26.

The food was very overpriced. Tried to sit in the lower down restaurant area as I have bad joints and cant sit on stools and got told that wasnt allowed if I was ordering from the bar. The food is very overpriced for what it is. The waiters are very rude and not at all helpful. They made me feel like I was a hindrance and I spent the whole time there wishing i went elsewhere for dinner. 

There are many more places in the area with better service and more reasonably priced food. It was not worth the stress it gave me for the expense it ended up being.

What did I just spend $250 dollars on? The overall meal and service was good but definitely not worth the price. The apps and sides were good but the steaks tasted like something I could have bought at Costco.

I would rate this place 3.5 stars.

Came here for lunch and I gotta say that the mojitos are soo good but way too strong for me (I can't handle anything, my husband had it).  They make them with pure sugar cane juice which makes them extra good, but they don't come cheap. I think it was about $13 for the mojito. 

We started off with the fire and ice ceviche which was good but really tiny.  It was quite expensive as well. I think about $15. Not worth the price.

I ordered the Plato Miramar salad which was: house smoked tuna, mojito-cured salmon, smoked duck breast, Serrano ham, queso blanco, sweet grape tomatoes, caper berries and marinated asparagus. Watercress and romaine salad, Spanish sherry vinaigrette.  This salad was good but a bit too salty because of all the meats and the caper berries. 

My husband ordered the good ole EL Cubano sandwich. The sandwich was delicious.

Beware of portion sizes and always ask for prices.I've been to this location for a late dinner with friends. Great decor and atmosphere.

Food quality is good but definitely not worth the price. The three of us all got something different and we all needed to get more food somewhere else after leaving even though we paid the same as we would for full sized entrees at other area eateries. 

A friend asked for a cheap wine recommendation and got hit with a bill for a $15 glass of wine. Yikes! Always ask of prices when a recommendation is offered.
Just.... Ok. I don't mind spending money on good food, but it really wasn't worth the price. Service was great.

They were so delicious and full of flavor and spice. 

Overall, the price point is very affordable but comes at a cost with the poor service. Would I come back again? Only if it requires a zero minute wait time.

The meal was really affordable as well. 

Coming back to browse the menu some without a doubt
Great food and wonderful experience! The only issue would be the price compared to portion size-- for the appetizers. The entree portions are generous and worth the price!

A nice variety on the menu with very reasonable prices. Went with a group of 4 and had 3 appetizers and 4 entrees for under $20 a person including tip. Food was flavorful although no additional sauces were on the table or offered. Although there were only a few other tables with customers felt rushed during dining. Overall a decent meal.

Food is quite good. 
Very reasonable prices.
Nuff said.

Off the beaten path, low key, great Philly Cheesesteak at Saad's in West Philly. The restaurant is tucked away in West Phila and there is only street parking. Also, be prepared that it is cash only up to $30. There is an  ATM for convenience in the back of the location for a $1 fee.  All drinks are bottled products but there is a great variety.

The food is very good. Enjoyed a cheesesteak with fried onions. Steaks traditionally come with mayo and ketchup which I am high on both for a Philly steak. The sandwich is a great size, is delicious and sits perfectly on a slightly toasted roll that does a great job to keep all the steak kept inside of the roll. 

Also tried a chicken shish tawook sandwich which was delicious. It is like a halal cart platter wrapped in a pita. Also available on a long roll.

The interior is dated and the seating gives off an '80s feel but the staff is very helpfu

I do not know why this restaurant doesn't have 5 stars or at least 4. This is a staple in the Chinatown community. Tell me somewhere else to eat for dim sum and I might judge you. They actually own Tom's too which I know other people go to but if you want a true, quality, and authentic experience of a family dim sum place, this is your place. They have the traditional clothed tables with the carts being pushed around. They also have tea typically served and make sure to tell them if you want the tea or not or there will be an upcharge as usual. I do not know what to recommend since it's in a different language and I cannot be bothered to translate but if it looks good on the cart while its passing or smells good, just get it. They take card but try to bring cash. They have wonderful service there and if there's something that you want that's NOT on the cart, just ask and they'll try to m

Overall, it was a really good experience. 
We bought tickets for the show, so we got there a bit earlier (with a reservation) to have dinner first. Then we had drinks while we enjoyed the music performance. 
The food was generally delicious. My husband said it was prob one of the best duck dishes he's had - I guess they were on point that night! the other entree choices were delicious as well. 
I'm still unsure of the whole process - the way we did it was prob best - bought tickets online, and reserved a table online for about an hour before the show - we got to stay at the table during the show. It seems that anyone who did not reserve a table had to stand. 
The downstairs - I don't even know how it works, but it was a more energetic show. Sometimes the music from downstairs could be heard, but overall the acoustics for the upstairs cafe (at least) was really nice.

Possibly the most genuinely nice and polite staff in Philadelphia!  The food is also quite good.  Definitely a step up from cheap Mexican... good full helpings, all entrees come with a tasty rice and beans, and they have a really nice assortment of maragaritas.  The free parking is also a really nice plus.  It's a little off the beaten path, but well worth a trip for a nice quiet meal, especially when the weather is nice as they have a nice outdoor patio.  Try the chorizo tacos... they're great!

Came in yesterday, as a first timer for an early lunch. I saw the place being built over the last month & wanted to give them a try. 

The establishment was clean & spacious. Enough room for the other customers ordering and/or dining in. The staff, one in particular was extremely pleasant & helpful. Being my first time there, I was staring at the menu & trying to figure out how to place an order.

The ordering is done on a touch screen, you pay there, & then a receipt is printed. It was fast & simple. I liked that. 

I ordered the Sweet Soy Five Spice. I enjoyed the meal very much. The green beans were crunchy, not mushy, the Turkey seasoned well, & I'm a bit of a spicy fan, so the sauce was just right. Overall a solid lunch. While I was eating, that same staff member checked on me, to see if I needed anything. In my book, their customer service was an A+.

Evidently a new "in" place judging from the dressed-up, excited crowd of thirty somethings.  Downstairs, a good looking decor with a big old school bar,  and comfy banquettes lining the walls.  Upstairs, a more utilitarian coffee bar, though with full drinks service, Italian-Style, made for a more peaceful place to  have a drink and wait for our reserved table to be ready.  Good professional service from the time the hostess came upstairs to get us through to Taylor, our (very) enthusiastic and efficient server.  We shared apps of Shrimp Scampi and a Caesar Salad, then ordered Chicken Parm, and the "Wild Boar" Bolognese.
Portions were generous but we both thought the general state of the offerings were ho-hum.  We appreciated the carafe of Nebbiolo at a very reasonable $36.00 considering the rest of the wine list was what I considered over-priced.

My husband and I live within walking distance of this diner, but only got to try it for the first time today.

I was a little nervous because there are a lot of negative reviews, but I was definitely pleasantly surprised! I also didn't know what the concept was behind the name, but apparently it's a diner filled with a bunch of celebrity mugshots. It's a little weird because I don't necessarily want to be thinking about criminals while I'm eating, but whatever.

Anyway, the food was good. I got the creme brûlée French toast and was a little trepidatious since diners don't usually tend to make sweet breakfasts too well, but I really enjoyed what came out! The French toast was pretty light and not too egg-y. My husband got a basic breakfast platter. It came with two eggs, home fries, toast, and meat. 

Our server kept our water and coffee/tea mugs filled, so that's a plus.

Cicala at the Divine Lorraine is a beautiful restaurant. We went on a Wednesday and had the entire restaurant to ourselves. While we had our vaccination cards/ID ready, we were never asked per the new city mandate. The food really was amazing, except...
...we had fruit flies swarming our table all night (they said they had "just sprayed" but they were back)
...the fritto misto antipasto didn't have half the items listed on the menu, the batter was unflavored and fat too thick. By the end, the thick rich sauce made the fried pieces limp and soggy (not to mention the sardines they added were still bone-in)
...the duck secondi was two pieces of duck (which was perfectly cooked, mind you) but NOT worth $43 (you should have received four pieces for that amount)

I came here for restaurant week with my boyfriend. The food was pretty good. The chefs did a wonderful job. My review would have been great, however there were 2 things that left a bad taste in my mouth. First, we asked to try (1) dumpling in case we wanted to order a side of it. They were nice enough to bring us one out with soy sauce. Well, when we went to pay the bill they charged us $2.00 for the sample and we were like "REALLY??? Going to nickle and dime us when we were already spending a lot???" Also, the waitress asked if we wanted coffee with our dessert and never mentioned a price. We saw that on the bill as well. I kind of could understand it, however it would have been nice if they mentioned there was a cost.

I'd gone to Vintage Wine Bar for wine once or twice in the past and usually left satisfied, but when I went in for an entire meal recently, the experience was much less satisfying.

I'm not sure if I went on a bad day or not, but the server was completely unfriendly and brash; it was the first bad impression that I received. Then, I ordered some mulled wine, which was much more "cinnamony" than some of the better mulled wines that I'd had in Europe, and I didn't find that too pleasing either. The whole affair didn't start too well -- I had to deal with a temperamental server and the overbearing taste of cinnamon in my mouth.

For dinner, I ordered some sort of burger and asked to have it cooked medium. When it came to me, however, the burger was burned to a cinder (and I am not exaggerating); the sauce on top of it was tasteless and the bun was also completely burned and black.

Portion sizes were very small for the prices, even for a health restaurant. 
However, very friendly employees, modern and welcoming atmosphere, and great quality and tasty ingredients.

What a disappointment this place was! We went there a couple of weeks ago for our anniversary. 
The atmosphere was nice - very trendy, but the food was hopeless. Expensive and mediocre bordering on downright bad. 
The menu is fussy and pretentious. 
Desert was ok I guess. Nothing special except the price tag. 

I have rarely been as disappointed with an expensive restaurant. 
Oh well, at least we know not to bother with this place ever again. You are much better off eating in China Town for a fraction of the price.

So after years of passing by, and hearing great things, i finally decided to stop in for a meal. 

So this was a first date, yelp says no to reservations, but when we walked in that was the question, not hello or welcome, but do you have a reservation? Luckily we brought wine which they opened directly for us to drink, otherwise we would've waited over 5 minutes for water. The seating situation it's really tight, so if your looking for privacy for a first date, it's probably not the place. The serving staff was very pleasant but kinda slow. 

We started out with some bruschetta which was just ok.
My date had the chicken picatta which she really enjoyed. I had veal saltimbocca which was awesome and the only reason I'm giving 3 stars. Then we has

Overall not the best place for a first date, luckily we had a blast anyway.

In terms of taste, this could be the best restaurant I've ever been to - ever. I mean, eating here was a sort of religious experience. I had better start from the beginning...

My wife and I went here for Valentine's Day this year. She really enjoys the Stephen Starr franchise, so I thought I would treat her to their flagship offering. While she absolutely loved it, I think that I enjoyed it as much as, if not more than, she did.

We went right after one of the huge snowstorms that hit Philadelphia this year, so we planned to valet park (so as to avoid snowbanking the car on the street or her ruining her shoes walking from a nearby garage). The valet parking was pretty steep at $24 (+tip), but it was worth it. Though, you should note that it is not in front of Barclay; it's down the block in front of Parc, so you will have to a walk a little.

First off, I'd like to say I've eaten here before, but never officially wrote a review so here it is now that I'm back again. 

Food - The options are pretty broad. They've got a selection of sushi, as well as ramen, and some appetizers and buns. I ended up getting the Shoyu Chicken Ramen. Honestly, I prefer my ramen to be less salty, I've tried a bunch of places that have the broth wayyy too salty, but Yamitsuki got it just right. 

Seating - I decided to sit at the tea bar, since I came alone. Since I say at the tea bar, I ordered the Iron Goddess of Mercy - Tie Guanyin Tea from Taiwan. I love trying different tea's, and I had never heard of this one, so I gave it a try. It's a pretty good tea to have if you enjoy green teas, it's got more of a leafy/herbal smell and taste, rather than a floral one.

Great date ambiance with dim lighting for good company. Highly recommend making a reservation as the tables can fill up quickly. 

The food has unique twists where they add flavors together that aren't traditional. It could be a hit or miss in my opinion. Some of out dishes were delicious while otherwise were.. interesting. I highly recommend the dinner rolls, the chive butter is amazing. We also ordered the fried chicken and the thai salmon. The salmon had a fresh spring of vegetables in a medium spicy sauce. The fried chicken portion was large. We weee not a fan of the collard greens, it was made way too sweet but the grits were really good. I recommend the potato frits as well. Those were a highlight!  

For dessert we had the dirty chai creme brûlée. It was good, chai is mild but unfortunately you can see its very burnt.
Really good food. portions are a little bit smaller but decent price and good flavor from what I got

It is a bit pricey for food that is just all right
Good for what it is and a nice ambiance!
The prices were really good for the amount of food you get. The atmosphere was well balanced as well. It was a pretty spot on place.

Great food! I found my new go-to place for a quick bite.  Food portions are on the smaller side but even after getting 3-4 things the total price was very reasonable.  Well worth it and will definitely recommend to my friends

I would give them two stars for the quality of the food but the portion size for the price is insane. They could be a bit more generous with the portion size. Do not eat here unless you have the stomach of a bird and like to waste money.

Really cheap, and this is the biggest advantage of this restaurant. But the food tasted...not that good. We ordered chicken noodle soup, fried beed dish and wonton soup, and both of us think that they are not delicious enough. But considered the price... it worths.

Food was definitely overrated. So was the experience.  It was nice being on the water, and the restaurant decor was nice, but it just wasn't all that great.  Service seemed annoyed the entire time like we were asking the waiter to do more than what his job entails.  High prices don't match the quality of the food, nor the service.. Oh well.

I give 2 stars as, the food is fairly good, not bad but, at these prices it just doesn't add up. Some things were very good, others not reasonably fulfilling when considering the prices. They really should do considerably better for pushing $200 for 2. I don't say this lightly and prefer to not speak badly but, feel it's fair to comment in this way all things considered.
Decent food, decent drinks, decent service. Went for restaurant week; portions were super small. Regular dinner menu is super pricy, not sure if it's worth the $$
