The food was decent but holy cow we spent way too much. This place is definitely overrated and just popular because of a popular name.

I recently made a date night reservation last minute and really enjoyed the place. I used to frequent a similar restaurant when I was in college so was very glad to stumble upon Rex 1516. 

It's a small dimly lit restaurant with fairly cozy seating--so be prepared to be close to your neighbor. I ordered the catfish which was really incredible. It had just the right amount of fry and flake. I also really enjoyed the hot sauce and crispy greens that come on top. When I ordered, the waitress kindly informed me the fish comes on top of the cold purée and beans. It really didn't bother me at all, but I enjoyed the heads up.

I also shared a crawfish pot pie with my partner. My god it was good. The crust is very buttery and the crawfish were cooked just right to not have a rubbery texture. 

The real show stopper was my partner's ham dish. That ham was probably the best ham I've ever eaten.
Good food and service. Portions are a little smaller than expected for the price.

Not as good as it's hyped up to be, but very nice ambiance, not crazy expensive, and good food. Was a bit disappointed by the lack of dessert options especially for a couple to share (the $16 one looked huge and the 2 other options were not too appealing.)
Nice ambiance and great tasting food. However the price and the portion size does not match.

This place was a little bit of a let down for me. I was so excited to finally go here but I don't know if I'll ever go back. It was my fiancé and I so we were seated at a small table for two. I'm fine with that but we were extremely close to the table of two beside us. The table was so close to us we could hear everything the people were saying next to us and the one girl would not stop talking. That was kind of annoying. Other than that, the place does have a really cool vibe. The lighting is dimmed and it has this relaxed but fun feel. Anyways about the food- we ordered a pitcher of Sangria which was really good. It was like a dry sangria instead of sweet. It was $32 but compared to other drinks on the menu being $9-$12 it made sense to go with this. Then we ordered the gnocchi off the menu and their special soft shell crab.
The food was decent, but way over-priced.  The restaurant was super loud and we felt rushed the entire time.

Hinge Cafe is a hidden gem in Port Richmond. Perfect brunch or breakfast spot especially after a church service on a Sunday. They close around 3:00 pm, but they are worth making sure to get there before they close! The ambiance has a vintage look and surprisingly there is a whole other room on the other side that accommodates larger parties than 4 people. They hang up local artwork which is kind of cool. The food is impeccable! I got a savory meal, which was the breakfast quesadilla with extra eggs and shared it with my friend, while she ordered the sweet which was the banana challah bread French toast. It was one of the best breakfast/Brunch meals I have had in a while. Definitely recommend this spot hands down for the food alone, but the staff was so polite and they didn't rush us out even though they were in the process of closing up for the day.

I had heard from a number of people that this place was amazing. I had dinner with a friend and we asked to be seated at the chefs counter, the chef greeted us and it was fun to look into the kitchen and watch the food prep. The kitchen sent us out two complimentary amuse bouches, a celery soup and raw tuna, both were very good. We shared 4 plates. The crab toast was served cold, which was a little disappointing but it was topped with lots of crab meat. The mushroom and whole wheat pasta with lemon sauce was decadent without being to heavy. The sea bass was a decent sized filet over a chunky fire roasted tomato and broccoli sauce, the chef was kind enough to give us a few pieces of perfectly grill sourdough bread to scoop up the sauce.

I think the thing that really impressed me about this place is the bang-for-your-buck factor. The food, while not extravagant, is very good, and it's less expensive than other restaurants of similar quality. My wife and I have been a couple of times and have had similar experiences each time.

I guess what comes to mind for me concerning this is that there are, yes, different strokes for different folks.

I will admit that I have a slightly skewed view on what makes a dining experience a pleasant one.  For instance, I believe that value is a integral part of a meal not in that cheaper is better but I don't really feel ripped off after eating a meal.  Also, service is not how much many times the server comes to your table but how they carry themselves when they do. 

In my mind, it's not important that a place looks nice or like a dump, if the food is expensive or cheap.  It's what the restaurant does with what they have that impresses me.  In that regard, this place kind of sucks.  It really feels like they are just phoning it in and charging out the ear for the privilege to eat there.

We went there yesterday for lunch since we were at a trade show at the convention center. We were going to grab a cheesesteak at the one spot down the isle from this place, but the line was too long so we grabbed the two seats available at Pearl's. We sat down and my first impression was MEH. The counter was dirty, which the waitress did eventually wipe down when she gave us the menus. The menu doesn't offer much, so not in a seafood mood, I went w/ the chicken tender platter. It came out in maybe 15 mins, not too shabby. Some of the fries were undercooked, some weren't. The chicken tenders were quite good. Not the run of the mill you get at a local bar or dinner. I can't comment on the cole slaw since I hate that stuff anyway. My lunch partner didn't complain about his fried oysters, so I'm guessing he enjoyed them (he tends to be picky). Overall it was pretty good.

We had just returned from a trip to Singapore, and I was hoping to get close to the delicious Malaysian food we had on the trip. Penang didn't disappoint, and was, in fact, quite true to the style of Malaysian food we had on the trip. 

The chicken satay is absolutely perfect. Made is fatty chicken thighs, the skewers bore the signature sweetness from the dry rub that one expects from a good satay. The dipping sauce was just the right consistency and had the right amount of heat too. Highly recommend. 

For our main courses, we had the Chow Kueh Teow and the Nasi Lemak. The chow kueh teow tasted just like the version we had at the hawker stalls in Singapore, and I enjoyed the beef that was included in the nasi lemak. I'm looking forward to coming back to try more of the food. 

Another bright spot of the meal is that the food is very inexpensive.

Off to a great start.  Three dishes were mind-blowingly great: a squash that had a complex, beautiful sauce; fried romanesco (like cauliflower) that was an excellent set of contrasts--fluffy milky cheese, bright mint, chilies, and the perfectly sized and fried cauliflower; and a dessert of some sort of berry tart, whose crust sang.  The signature fig and blue cheese ravioli was also a textural and flavor delight, albeit a fairly rich one.   Extremely knowledgeable service, and a very pleasingly warm room.  The pacing of dishes coming out of the kitchen seems off, and hence not 5 stars -- some came too quickly, some too late, and at tables next to me, the courses seemed too rushed together (entrees served before apps done).  They also don't seem to have the right formula estimating table turning time.
The portions were smaller than expected. However the dining environment was serene. And the food that was made with perfection. Taste wasn't disappointing but proportion was...
Great ambience and service, however, food was not worth the price! A little disappointed.

Brought some out of town coworkers here and boy was I disappointed. They always rely on me to suggest great restaurants and this failed me so much!

The only memorable item I can get in 5 other places and that was the cannoli at the end of the meal. We did the chef's tasting which in my opinion was weirdly laid out. 2 apps, 1 salad, 1 side, 1 pasta and 1 protein. It just didn't seem balanced. We got:

- shrimp scampi which may have been the best out of everything
- the meatballs were eh
- ceaser salad was one of the worst come on guys panera can do better
- Roasted peppers (the whole side section was mediocre at best as far as offerings) tasted like they were jarred
- The gnocchi (in red sauce), oh lawd it tasted so bland and sad. I think it was supposed to have sage too which it didn't
- Chicken Parm - the second best thing.
This was not a bad experience, but the food was not as good as expected especially for the price. We got two all you can eat buffets and cost $75.... way too much.

Good for a casual date night, but I wasn't impressed.  

This is what me and my date shared:

A pitcher of the Sangria (Rojo)---this was yummmmy!
A shot of Mezcal-very smooth
An order of Guacamole---$10 bucks for a huge bowl of what seemed of pureed (yet a bit chunky) avacado, but once you taste it, the flavors of lime and cilantra come out.  They're a bit subtle, but makes for good guac. Topped with queso blanco??? We think.
Short Rib Enchiladas- Good, but the sauce they were drenched in didn't really have any kick to it, just seemed like regular tomato sauce
Carnitas Tacos--Three 3-inch soft shelled tacos packed with meat (cooked very well, no complaints here) and cilantro.

Overall it was a good meal.  Didn't leave there feeling unsatisfied or overly stuffed.

Overall rating 'Just good'.  A little pricey for dining in a converted row house. Not very comfortable.

Service great!  Food is good but not worth the price.

I don't appreciate 'cash only' restaurants.

Too fancy pants, portions are way too small, price is way too big. 

Classical trendy restaurant that serves good food, but not worth the price. Trying to impress the girl on the first place? Most of the other people here too.

Overall the food was pretty good. I thought for $35 I would get a decent sized piece of halibut but it was very small and not worth the price IMO. The chicken liver mouse was pretty lackluster. More of a liver taste than a buttery smooth taste like goose liver. $31 for a dozen oysters is also laughable. Menu is on the small side, which is why I wouldn't go back. A decent place but overpriced and small portions.

Save your money!  Not worth the price for the amount of food that is served.  Also, the service was subpar.  Our meals took forever to come to the table.  However, the ambiance is really cool.  I think more time needs to be spent on service and increasing meal portions rather than adding another flower box to the wall.

They plates for ridiculously small for an unreasonable price. For dessert we ordered three out of the 4 available desserts which were all good but microscopic.   Each dessert was the size of one scoop of ice cream.  The service we agreed was also "just ok" and the menu is confusing.  The menu options dont explain or help you visualize what the dish actually is and we had a lot of questions.  Due to the price and a 5 star image, I was disappointed to spend $300 for dinner and leave kinda hungry and not fully satisfied.   The food tasted good but not worth the price at all.
Overpriced food that really isn't worth the money. A salad with chicken is $17.00. Great atmosphere, really cool outdoor space, but not worth the price.
It's also way overpriced for the quality of food.

I came here on a Friday night for dinner. The atmosphere is very homey feeling and it feels as if you're sitting in someone's apartment eating. It is pretty tight quarters inside. We sat just inside the door in the first room, so I am not sure if other rooms/seating areas are bigger. 

I ordered the Greek sausage dish and my girlfriend ordered the veggie stuffed peppers. Overall the meal was good. It was nothing extravagant or special however. It did taste homemade which was nice and authentic. Both of our meals came with a lot of rice, which is good, but for the price I would have liked a little more substance. The Greek sausage dish consists of sliced sausages in a marinara sauce with sautéed peppers over rice. It was tasty, but for $19 is a bit overpriced in my opinion. 

Overall the meals were good, but nothing special. It is very Greek and tasted authentic which was nice.
Bottom line:  overrated and overpriced, couldn't believe I saw so many relatively young people dining in here

The food is tasty, but nothing stood out as particularly tremendous and it was overpriced.  The service was efficient and very friendly, and it certainly wasn't a bad experience, but not worth repeating at these prices.  The tables near the end give a nice view, but if you're seating farther into the restaurant there isn't as much to see.
Overpriced for the quality. I ordered the pasta the food was delicious but the quantity was very minimal

Not bad. Expensive but not bad. Does seem a little overpriced though for what is worth. Good definitely but I would expect a larger size of food for the price we were paying. Not Rly enough in that area. Good food overall though.

really expensive for small portions. Food was good. But...but, it was not up to the standard one would expect for the price. Just not satesfying. Also, the music and ambiance was very simple and blah. The decor was nice and eclectic.

Great decor and environment for drinks but the food is really lacking.
I'd come here to hang out any night still but only if I ate beforehand. 

The food is very over priced and just not that exciting. Greasy, sloppy food. Perhaps it would taste better at half the price. 

I really want to like the place as the ambiance is so great but I just cannot get over the ridiculous prices.

So expensive for mediocre food! I wasn't expecting authentic and had set a low bar to begin with. However the food is just not very good or  substantial. Their happy hour prices should be their regular prices across the board. My bill was $25 just for me and I left hungry.
Not worth the hype. The portion size of the pasta plates is laughable. Overpriced for the quality and portion size.
Great service, delicious food, good ambiance, but a bit overpriced.
You're definitely paying for the experience which is amazing! The food is pretty good but not worth the price you pay. Service is very good!!

Food is rich, but in the way that makes you feel like ugh afterwards.
Overpriced. Loud, drunk people at the front. Tries to be fancy, but really, isn't.

In summary: overpriced, overcrowded, and wasteful! The food might be okay, but it's NOT worth the price tag. Maybe worth it for a coffee/pastry (I didn't try that part of the restaurant) but not for the food. 

I thought this would be a really neat gourmet cafe/cafeteria type place. The concept is trying to get there but it's not. First of all, it's so overpriced. I paid $15 for a small REHEATED piece of salmon and potato soup. SOUP. 1 to 2 stars down for overcharging me for reheated food. 

For the price point, you're better off having a sit down lunch/brunch somewhere in the Gayborhood. This isn't super quick either (because you have to wait for your food to be reheated) and it was hard for my party of 3 to find a place to sit. It's seat yourself  community seating but there aren't enough places to sit. 

Even more importantly, the way it all works is so wasteful!

Everything was nicely cooked and seasoned, but it was just a good steak and a good piece of fish, not worth the price for sure.

Very expensive, one of the more expensive meals I have ever had in the city and not worth that price. May be next time, drinks and some gnocchi

I went here for dinner with some friends. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, although the space was a little more cramped than I was expecting. The staff was pleasant and helpful, nothing spectacular. My take on the food is that it was good and well prsented, but definitely not worth the price they are charging.
Not worth the price. Staff was extremely friendly, but the food on the trough wasn't worth it.
Below average tasting food. Service was fast but not worth the price. No seating at this location.
Food not worth the price. Minimum spending per person is insulting for what's being served.

Also, it was fairly affordable for what I ordered. 

Definitely check this place out!

Definitely affordable, with all dishes ranging from $6-8, with soups/ sides well under this price. The dishes are all pre- made, so you are not getting your own "batch". The food is good but you are getting what you pay for.

I got the Spicy shrimp with bamboo shoots, but I think I will try a curry if I head back. People ahead of me/ behind me ordered curry and it looked great.
So we did take out and were very pleasantly surprised. The food was delicious, the portions good, and reasonably priced! Our expectations were definitely exceeded!
Food was delicious and portion was plentiful with affordable price. The service was also nice and friendly

Anyone who thinks the food here is worth the price is smoking crack.  First time dining here will be the last.  The waitress recommended 3-4 orders per person.  We had a party of 3 and ordered 7 total dishes (so less than what she recommended).  This cost us $39 per person (including tax and tip).  $39!

Now, I'm not against high prices if it's spent wisely (Alma de Cuba, Amada, Le Bec Fin, to name a few).  But the portions for these small plates are unacceptably tiny.  

Small portions, high prices--fine, I'll deal with it if the food is awesome.  It wasn't.  Just FYI, we had the lobster roll, crab tacos, Peking duck, Korean short ribs, Korean rice cake, and Ma Po tofu, and "Philly Cheesesteak".  The only thing that was actually good was the Philly Cheesesteak, crab tacos, and Korean short ribs.  Sadly, the dishes were NOT so good as to justify the ridiculous price.

I ordered the stuffed meatball, which was very good and reasonably priced. When I received my meal I realized that the relatively low price was due to the smaller than average portion size. As a small person, It was a satisfying portion for me and I didn't leave overstuffed; However, my friend was still a little hungry at the end of the meal, although he enjoyed his steak. 
The restaurant lighting was very dim, which can be nice and romantic, but in my opinion it was slightly too dark for what I like in a restaurant.
Overall, wonderful experience, food, and service. Only downside is the portion size, but the price makes it worth it.

Yeah, totally minor and not even worth mentioning, so I probably shouldn't have since it just makes me seem like a jerk. 
Our waitress was very nice, perfectly attentive, just awesome really. She did a pretty wonderful job. We really wanted for nothing for 95% of our visit. 

Drinks: We each had a cocktail while we waited/during the appetizer. I had a Jack & Ginger and mom had a Jameson & Ginger. They were perfectly made. Well, perfectly made for me, but I like a strong-ish drink where you can actually taste the alcohol. 

Wine: We ordered a bottle of Malbec. It was reasonably priced at around 37 dollars. It was tasty. Granted, I could have picked up the same bottle for around 20 (and have in the past), but it still wasn't completely out of line. 

Food: 
So it starts with these biscuit things and butter. The biscuits look like they should be cheddar biscuits, but sadly, they weren't.

This place was pretty good and has very nice decor.  The servings were not big enough, but everything was pretty tasty.  Somebody at a table near us got the tasting menu that is offered.  It was more expensive than if you ordered a la carte, but looked much more plentiful.  All things considered, I would not run back here.  I think that more authentic versions of this food can be found elsewhere and at much more reasonable prices.

Food and service were terrific. BBQ oysters, grilled octopus, sauteed fresh flounder. However, the loud noise ruined our dinner. My friend from NY said it was the loudest restaurant she has ever been in. Even our waitress said she had to read lips. We would not return unless they improve acoustics.

The food was good particularly the kale salad and the steak, but what got me was the noise of the music and the conversation of many others to the detriment of my being able to hear the person across the table from me. If I go out to a restaurant, I think the least the establishment can do is provide me a place to be able to communicate with fellow dinners. The dessert was so small as to be....a taste of a cake and fig ice cream. I will not go back.
I think they should investigate improving the acoustics of the space. There are too many hard surfaces and nothing to deaden the sounds.
Good good, nice space- but what really stands out is how LOUD it is. I am no crotchety old woman, but when I can't hear any of the dinner conversation, that is a problem.

The noise level in this restaurant makes it virtually impossible to hold a conversation. Low light level made reading the menu a challenge. If you can get past those obstacles you will find the food a delight and the service efficient and friendly.

The food is quite good, and the free chips and salsa are fresh, tasty, and plentiful.  Service is consistent, fast, and suprisingly attentive given the always rapid pace.

Did I mention the fab margarita selection?  If there are two or more of you it's definitely worth getting a pitcher... if you don't mind the buzz you'll carry out with you afterward.  Blood Orange is my fave, but I recently had the Cucumber and it was really interesting and perfect for a hot summer day.

If you've ever had tacos at a legit taqueria you will be slightly disappointed with Cantina's version, however.  Close to the real thing but not quite.  The burrito's won't set the world on fire either, but they are pretty good and you certainly get a lot of food for the price.

Place was so loud it was to the point of being startling.  Had a loud ass four top of Millennials next to us who kept shouting over each other.   We were packed into the back room when there was ample seating available upstairs which we didn't notice until we walked out.   Food was meh... Hard to eat when you're being subjected to ear torture.   Recommendation is to install some sound deadening material on the walls or tell people to shut the f*ck up.

We just stumbled across this place while looking for somewhere to eat near our hotel. It looked cute on the outside, but it was a total circus on the inside. There is a bar, and a couple of dining areas, but unfortunately they all seemed to converge right where we were sitting, meaning that our table was constantly being pushed past by everyone, which made for a very poor, very hassled dining experience. Even worse was the ear-splitting noise. This place was so loud, my friend and I had to shout at each other across our small table, and ended up downing our drinks and packing up our food just so we could get out of there before any permanent hearing loss occurred  (hopefully).
I've been here a few times.  I think the food is good not great.   My biggest complaint is the noise level.  When the place is full it's incredibly loud and hard to have a conversation.

Positive: Mostly good food.
Negative: Holy cr@p, it is loud!  Even with the restaurant only 2/3 full, you have to scream to make the person next to you hear what you're saying.

My boyfriend and I had dinner reservations at XIX Nineteen to celebrate our anniversary. I was initially very excited to have dinner here, because of the gorgeous view and the great reviews I read online.  However, when I got there, it was anything but amazing.

When we made the reservation (almost a month ahead of time), we requested to sit near a window, but when we got to the restaurant we were told that they didn't have anything available.  That was clearly a lie, because there were multiple tables near windows in the main dining room.  Strike number one.

Our waiter seemed very nice at first.  However, when he realized we weren't spending money on appetizers or alcohol, his whole demeanor changed.  I don't expect A+ service all the time, but if we're spending $100+ at a restaurant, I want my waiter to be happy and pleased to serve us. Strike two.

El Vez has great guacamole and chips, the chicken tacos are delicious and the shrimp enchiladas are amazing but I will never go back because the noise level was horrendous. My husband and I had important plans to discuss but were unable to have even a simply conversation. It's so loud everyone in the restaurant is shouting including the waitresses.
The food isn't worth the noise!

My wife and I dine here this past Saturday night.  We had an early reservation, but the place was already full, both on the first floor and second floor.  Each floor has a bar with a nice selection of liquor and an outstanding selection of wines.  Service was excellent.  The menu, although limited, was creative and the food was good.  Not great, but good.  The reason for the low rating is that the noise level is extreme.  The walls, ceilings and floors are all hard surfaces, with nothing to absorb sound except for patrons' clothing.  The prices are relatively high, but I wouldn't have cared that much if the entire experience had been enjoyable -- which it wasn't.  What good is a good restaurant where you can't talk?  We will never go back.

A hard review to write, as i loved the food and thought that our server was fantastic. But, this was without any doubt, the single loudest restaurant that I've ever been to. It was loud enough to significantly effect my experience. 

If you are in anyway sensitive to noise or, if like me, just simply prefer a quieter atmosphere, this is by no means an option.

I've been here before. Food and margs are decent, but the noise level was UNCOMFORTABLY LOUD! I HAD TO MOVE MY CHAIR TO THE SIDE IN THE HOPES I COUKD HEAR MY DINNER COMPANION. IT DIDN'T WORK! When I asked the waiter if it was always this loud on a Friday night, he shrugged and replied, "If people are talking loudly." A trip through the restaurant to the bathroom confirmed it was loud everywhere. SO APPARENTLY PEOPLE TALK LOUD AT THE BAR, IN A DINING ROOM.... If you go, go on a warm evening and sit on the patio if you would like to have a conversation that isn't punctuated by "Huh?" and "What?".

The food is awesome, but it is so incredibly loud there it's not a very pleasant place to eat. I came for a date with my boo, and we had to scream at each other above the din. It was hard to relax and enjoy the food, because it was impossible to have a conversation. It is pretty crowded (easy to bang elbows with your neighbor) and that doesn't help the noise sitch since you can hear them screaming as well. Maybe if I was at the bar for a lively drink it would be fun, but the care put into the food is not matched by care put into the experience of eating the food.

We ate at Zahav for the first time, but I was familiar with Solomonov's recipes from his wonderful cookbook. The incomparable braised lamb shoulder with chickpeas and pomegranate molasses glaze has been a star at three different company meals in our home. It is amazing!
   We were too late to order that this trip--they run out early--but we got the tasting menu which is just incredible. The salads, hummus, and bread are enough for a whole meal, but then come the mezzes, entrees, and desserts. Thankfully, the entrees are smaller than the mezzes! That is something I never thought I would hear myself say. The service was great. 
   My one complaint--and it is a BIG one because it kinda ruined the evening--is the phenomenally loud music being piped. We complained twice, and it got marginally better.

I've been to this location a number of times, and have to agree it's been slipping in quality and service.  We went on a Friday night, and I have to say it was, hands-down, the loudest restaurant I've ever been to.  Not their fault, just what it is.  There were a number of large groups of what appeared to be students, and every one of these groups was obnoxiously loud.  Not just talking, but screaming, singing, etc.  It started to resemble a loud frat party.  The staff were working hard, and running around like lunatics trying to keep things moving.  This created a frenetic atmosphere, and both people and staff were pushing past our table, and on occasion, knocking things off the table.  It was a chaotic scene, to say the least.  We waited about 20 minutes for our reserved table.  

The food ranged from just OK to pretty good.

Great service and interesting food that we would like to explore, however, the noise level is unsettling. We were there on a week night with place 1/3 filled and our group of 6 had a hard time hearing conversation. It's disappointing for a newly constructed facility to not have considered sound dampening aspects. Hopefully the owners can correct this.

It's name says it best, "YUM, YUM". 
As other reviews have mentioned this place is a little pricey but c'mon you are saving on liquor since its BYO and you are experiencing creative sushi rolls beyond the "specialty rolls'" common to most sushi restaurants.  Treat yourself to the Godzilla roll, although the $16 price is big (like you'd expect the actual monster to be) the roll is delicious combination of nuts, avocado, strawberries and shrimp tempura.  Service is slow but in this recent case, the staff was professional enough to realize and help us kill time  (and hunger) with complimentary edamame.  It does have a super datey feel to it, so if you are going with a friend sit at the bar and watch the chef Alexander McCoy (formerly of Morimoto and Colorado based, Teikoku) work his magic.

We were very pleased to get a lovely booth when we arrived. Our server was excellent and the food terrific. The restaurant is very attractive and inviting. However, the restaurant is SO NOISY that we had difficulty conversing and enjoying our meal. There was loud rock like music on the sound system which does not go with such a fine restaurant. In addition there were large groups nearby that added to the noise. It is unfortunate and we would never return. The Prices are VERY high. It is just not worth it.

The food was excellent, the waiter was excellent.  Our issue was with the noise level.  It was difficult for my wife and I to have a conversation.  It was a combination of the decor (hardwood floors) and the other restaurant patrons.  We we surrounded with loud-mouthed diners, who spoke far too loud.  The restaurant needs to move and not tell the current patrons where they are going.  We would go back for the food and service, but are reluctant due to the clientele.

too loud!  will not go again.  a 1:30 lunch should have been more quiet.  however, the music was blaring, to add to the noise level.  dining with friends to me means a chance to talk and eat good food.  talking was painful.  we had to shout to be heard.  and this was at a table in the front by the window.  it should have been more quiet that it was.
food can be great, but not worth the $$, in absense of ability to converse with friends.

Yes the restaurant is noisy but honestly, do you really expect to sit in a quiet restaurant on a weekend night? I did have to speak above my normal volume but I still didn't feel like I was shouting. I will definitely be back to El Vez, and soon!

Food is cool service and atmosphere is lousey. And very loud i asked to move seating twice and still a particular group of patrons was very loud with no one to ask them to quiet down a bit... the ppl who dined here that night were very upset.

When the place I wanted to go for lunch was closed, I decided to try this place.  It was great to find a restaurant with a lot of veggie-based, but not all strictly vegetarian or vegan, options.  The salad I had (Wild Child) was excellent.  The rest of the menu looks great too.  But one thing kept me from giving it 5 or even 4 stars:
WHY IS THE MUSIC SO LOUD!!!!?

I like music.  In fact, I love music.  I play music. I go to music events.  I have accepted that no restaurant can tolerate, or thinks its customers can tolerate, a quiet background.  So, there's music. But this was so loud it made me feel anxious and rush my meal. Is that what restaurant management wants?  There's no need in this case, because it wasn't at all crowded, I could have lingered and relaxed without a tiny bit of guilt over making others wait for a table.  But yet I couldn't, because it was too loud.

Been several times as it is by my house and has big tables that are easy to work at.  But, I am thinking of not going back.  Its constantly very loud inside and the manager / owner is rude.  Most of the other staff is nice, albeit one of them is constantly talking loud behind the counter and is just obnoxious.  Would like it more if it was a little more quite and peaceful to work at.

A quiet Sunday dinner???- NOT AT FORK. Why? Crowded? No-half empty. Loud guests? No. Sound system volume excessive? YES. Polite request x 3 to turn it down ignored despite complaints from other patron(s). If you like to shout at your companion for the entire dinner due to the overly loud music, this is the place.

While the food and service were quite good, there are numerous other establishments that provide fine food and an ambiance that does not reflect the arrogance of the establishment.
Great atmosphere, food and drinks. We were sitting upstairs and it was really quiet which was great cause we could easily talk. Everyone was really nice to us, no complaints
So disappointed! Certainly not a quiet place for conversation and enjoying those you're with. The volume of music and loud talk really made me dislike the food. Would not hurry to go back.

Tried this place for the first time. The noise levels absolutely ruined the experience for us and it was supppsed to be a special birthday night! Not a place to come for a quiet date night or even if you just want to have a conversation with someone. There was so much noise with the party next to us, it ruined this experience for us. The waitress was sympathetic and the food was yummy, but I'll think twice before coming back here. The noise was really that bad folks!

All in all good food but vastly overrated given the hype. I might have guessed...but still. And I do have two MAJOR complaints. 
One waitress, the head person in the dining room,  is so obnoxiously loud that I could almost not finish my meal. She stood next to our table bellowing out comments on the food to the table right next ours (I suspect it is the person who reviewed below), a couple of self-professed foodies who kept asking her about every dish. She came back at least four times, each time for a ten minute conversation--thereby ignoring the rest of her guests. Aside from the fact that her butt was facing me most of that time (as in ten inches away from my head), the volume and inanity started to seriously get on my nerves. All the more annoying that this was delightfully quiet dining room. Excessive noise, especially in a high end place, is one of my pet peeves.

Heard this place was good so why not give it a try. Came here last night for a friends birthday. 

Noise level was extremely loud that my friends and I couldn't hear each other talking. Our server was yelling as she was explaining the menu to us. If you want a nice quiet dinner, this place is definitely not it. If you want to scream at each other during dinner then this is the place.

Our server was very rude and kept messing up our order. When we told her we didn't order these food items she said my friends and I didn't communicate correctly because she heard someone order this.. when the food got to our table we all claim our entree but there were 4 extra items that we did not order. The server kept saying someone ordered this and we should figure out who ordered what and not blame the server. She mention it was her job to take orders, not figure out who ordered what.

Reserved for two at 6 PM. Wanted as much quiet as Vernick could provide. On arrival told the lovely hostess the same and she seated at a pleasant table in the room adjacent to the kitchen. Looked like a fine spot and during the first first course or two the ambient sound remained reasonably quiet. However once things warmed up in the adjacent bar area, a dull roar of people noise took over making it literally impossible to have a conversation with my dinner partner.  

Of course everything we value in fine dining was present in spades. The food was incredible and the service excellent. Too bad the sound diminished the pleasure of the occasion. 

Vernick: you need an accoustical redo of your space!! But otherwise  don't change a thing.

In brief, I recommend. The building was lovely and spacious. The food was very good, the servings were huge, and the waitstaff professional and competent. All around very good. The only thing I wanted to note specifically was this appeared in a Yelp list of "quiet restaurants near center city, Philadelphia" and--at least last night, around 6 pm--it was anything but quiet. At a table of four, I had a lot of difficulty hearing. So, if you are looking for quiet conversation, this may not be a good spot. Otherwise, go and enjoy!
Food was good and the service was awesome but get ready to yell over everyone else. It's so fucking loud I don't think I would come back.

The place looked so cute for a date night. But the ambiance was ruined by a few things. First minor thing was being sat towards the back because the bright light from the kitchen canceled out the dark romantic lighting (see pic with arows pointing to bright light coming from kitchen). The most disruptive thing was one of the managers. Like most managers he went around talking to customers and asking about their dining experience. But he talked SO LOUD and for SO LONG. My date and I considered asking being moved because his loud voice talking about himself and the restaurant was so annoying even though we were on the opposite side of the restaurant and behind dividers. I hope someone tells him it's great to be friendly but don't overstay your table visits and for goodness sake, don't talk so loudly. 

The food was ok. I prefer trattoria caterina.
Everything was great. The only downfall to the restaurant would be the really loud live music. I could barely hear over my friends and we were literally 3 feet apart at most.

I was very impressed with this fine Italian establishment! From the moment I walked in, to the moment the wait staff bid me farewell, I was treated with respect and dignity and thanked copiously for my patronage.

My girlfriend recommended this establishment as a welcome back dinner for a trip I was returning from. She stated that she had been to the other location further down the street, and that she felt this location would be a great comparison. Immediately upon being seated, we were greeted by the wait staff and asked if they could pour us a glass of the white wine we brought with us (this location is a BYOB). The menu options left me thinking at how I could choose from such a smorgasbord of delicious meals. I was very impressed with the poultry dishes that we all ordered.

(On a Friday night,. First time here. Stumbled on it using Yelp.) Ok, so I chose this place bc it was vegan as I have recently decided to make some eating lifestyle changes. And i like to try places I've never been before. I chose well... So I didn't realize this place was right in the heart of an area that I frequent. So many good places and now I have yet another to choose from. Place was very busy, mind you not a huuge place but comfortable. Ambiance is right in my wheel house. Dim, speak easy type of place. If you're into cocktails and lounging this is it and it's easy to jump to another place from here if you're so inclined but I could easily spend an evening here. Imo. 

I made it 10mins before happy hour ended which is at 7p. I wss greeted by the very amicable Pete. He helped me w drink choice based on what i liked and he was very meticulous about finding the right flavor". I ende

Great experience all around.  We tried so much food we never tried before and it was all wonderful.  The acoustics were great.  That sounds weird but I could actually have a nice conversation without all the ambient noise that is so common in restaurants these days.

The food, the staff, the service here are all very good.  But if you're looking for a place to enjoy a conversation while you eat then this is NOT the place for you.  The music inside is nightclub-level loud.  Nobody else seemed bothered by it so maybe I'm an outlier but for that reason I won't be going back.

This restaurant is NOT for the hard of hearing! The acoustics inside this place are terrible, and once the volume of people inside gets high enough, we couldn't even hear the people in our own party talking across the table. We ended up leaving because my father who has a hearing aid was completely helpless. The food is absolutely divine, however. Some of the best Italian I've had in the states. If any of your party is hard of hearing, though, you may unfortunately have to go somewhere else:(

If ain't broke, don't worry about it. Restaurant Week at Melograno is LOVE. This is my second RW dinner here and while everyone else is going off menu, Melograno has options on top of options and they are all delicious. Meatballs with a perfect sauce. A lamb dish where the meat fell right off the bones. Even my guest cleaned the whole bowl with her charcuterie salad. The flan dessert was so rich and we were so full that we couldn't even finish it. Still, a great RW deal. The staff was helpful. We had the last seating of the night and the manager still stopped by to speak while topping our wine glasses off. He did not HAVE to do that because the server was on it already. That attention to detail--at 11:30pm, no less--is appreciated. There's only one downside to Melograno: it's loud as hell!

Solid coffee and pastries, but this was the loudest coffee shop I've ever experienced (and I'm not exactly picky about noise).  The music was loud.  The patrons were loud.  Even the dishwasher was loud with the stacking of the clean plates.  It was like there was a competition amongst everybody to see who could be the loudest.

Grabbed an early dinner here after reading all the rave reviews. I guess the one thing I missed in those reviews was how LOUD it is. It's loud talk, low yell kind of loud, at least in the upper area where we were. Seriously... My wife and I joked that this is a good place for married couples but not for a date because there is no chance of having any kind of conversation across the table. And that is despite being almost elbow to elbow with the next table.

Food was very good and the service was attentive and friendly.

This seems like a good gathering spot for a small group of good friends who want to laugh and enjoy dinner and aren't concerned with yelling across a table, but I wouldn't bring a client or a (first) date here.

We eat here a few times a year - live in the neighborhood but have about 100 other choices in the few blocks between us and them otherwise would be much more frequent.  The food is really outstanding, especially the homemade pasta dishes.  Service is great too, and BYO makes it great value for what you get, even if a few of the entrees are priced in the high side (but our 2 app 2 pasta 2 dessert dinner totaled $88).  Last night I strayed outside the usual standards like the boar ragu ... and had (you're not going to believe this) a cocoa pasta with goat and goat cheese ragu... NOT something I would make at home, and it was utterly delicious.  As were our appetizers and desserts- sambuca panna cotta YUM.

Ate here on a Saturday morning, wait was only about 15 minutes which I didn't think was that bad for a weekend at 10am. After leaving by roughly 11:30 a long wait had manifested outside, probably better to get in before 10am on the weekends. Service was great, our waitress was very attentive and friendly, dining room was crowded, a bit difficult to hear due to echo of the old building. I loved the cute chalkboard skeleton drawing. I ordered the heuvos rancheros and the lavender blueberry lemonade. The lemonade was delicious, a bit sweet but it had the perfect balance of flavors, I'd definitely get it again. The huevos rancheros was decent, I felt it lacked in flavor a tad. I tried the peach French toast special, also very good and the peach definitely tasted fresh.

Good food and attentive service; however, bring ear plugs. By far, the loudest restaurant that I have ever dined. The place does a great business but the rooms are so tight; you rub elbows with the table behind you.
The food was excellent! The service was great. The place is beautiful. But... It was so loud I couldn't hear. Like at all . Not a word. I ruined the experience .

My girlfriend and I were very excited to eat here. The pictures of the hand drawn noodles is enough to make anyone want to try this place out. We ordered beef brisket soup along with the spicy pig ears. In my opinion, the pig ears were a bit overpriced, but they were still tasty nonetheless. They had just the right amount of spice and the bit of chewiness matches the radish slaw underneath. This unique dish is definitely a must try! The soup was fantastic as well. Considering the price of the order, they gave us a huge serving of noodles and beef. If you're not a big eater, I recommend you first share a bowl with someone else to avoid over-ordering. Anyway, the noodles were fresh and the broth was served steaming hot and was very flavorful. 
This place has amazing authentic food that's high quality. The service is very fast as well!

Visited on a Saturday evening to have dinner.  Food was OK, burgers were reported by others at the table to be good.  Noise, like many Philly small restaurants, was over the top, even more over the top than most.  Sustained over 90 decibels the whole time, going over 100 decibels when some guy at the bar wanted to talk to his buddies.  No attempt at noise management in the decor.  Left with a headache.  Bye bye, never again.

Let me start by saying that the reviews that rave about the delicious food are all true. The food is beautiful, loaded with flavor, spice and everything nice. The mom's khao yum kamin salad was so flavorful with coconut, dried shrimp, vegetables, chili flakes.. served at the table with a beautiful presentation of each item placed in the dish separately and the server comes to mix the bowl. This salad with its flavor and texture was delightful. The fried rice along with the crab coconut curry was rich and depth-filled. I ordered the shrimp with glass noodles by recommendation from our server and she did not steer me wrong. The dish is infused with flavor then baked in a pot. I'm telling you, the shrimp was huge and meaty and almost tasted like I was eating hearty pieces of crab (and that's a good thing).

The food is great but if you are dining to also enjoy a having a conversation with someone, go elsewhere. This restaurant routinely welcomes very large groups who bring lots of wine and drink way too much. The large groups of young folks have on three separate occasions (!!) been obnoxiously LOUD and rowdy. The restaurant management takes no action. Will not return because it feels like a frat house and not a restaurant. Too bad - good food but horrible experience

Food and service is EXCELLENT.  My only complaint is the noise level due to the music that they blast. Found myself yelling across the table while trying to have a conversation with my dining companion. If they lowered the music, this would be my favorite restaurant in the city. Hands down.

This restaurant was highly recommended by some of our colleagues, but unfortunately, we find it to be vastly overrated, and positively repugnant in many respects.  First, the atmosphere - it was touted by our friends to be ultra-modern.  Ultra-modern if you come from the 1960s and from an unsophisticated class - in the genre of lava lamps and gaudy lights in pale imitation of Andy Warhol.  What was most horrible was the noise level - supposedly the windowless tubular space with bare plastic furniture and walls were supposed to resemble the innards of a whale (with you about to be digested by Morimoto).  Anyway, I had to resort to my iphone's itunes piped into my ears to escape from the noise assault.   Poor servers who have to endure this assault to their hearing every day and night!  The food was, um, very uneven.

This place has decent food, and it's a nice addition to the neighborhood, but they play the music SO LOUDLY that you can't even hear the person sitting next to you, let alone anyone sitting across the table. We would honestly come here more If it wasn't so loud.

Amazing venue I had the opportunity to visit during CCD Restaurant Week. The dining room is indeed loud with conversations echoing throughout the space but that helped mask my convo from that of my neighbors. So while seating is squeezed in, the noise level sort of acts like a cocoon to still make your dining table feel intimate and separate from the rest of the room. The staff was helpful and attentive and clearly work well as a team. One server clearing plates while another delivered the next coarse all while their colleague is uncorking my bottle of red blend wine. All of this is close proximity and with a smile. That's no easy feat during the rush of Resto Week and they should be commended for it.

I went here Sunday evening with my boyfriend as it is his current favorite pizza place in his neighborhood. Pietro's pizza is delicious. The crust is crispy on the outside and fluffy inside, just like roman bread. If you've been to Rome, you know what I'm talking about. The odd thing is that their bread basket is not the same quality. Perhaps they have some hack bakery deliver these? If they are made in house, get the guy/girl who makes the pizza dough to share their tips, please! 

In any case the pizza toppings are fresh, and good quality. We enjoyed a pizza with arugula and proscuito. Delish.

The other downside is that the bus boy staff needs to be trained like the waiters/waitresses. We asked for a cruet of balsamic vinegar only to have it taken back 5 minutes later for another table. Did Pietros only have one cruet of vinegar for the entire restaurant? Seemed quite odd.

It's a little expensive, but I enjoyed Amada.  The food was very good.  We got the chef's selection tasting menu.  We had no idea what was coming next, or even if there was more food coming.  That meant I didn't pace myself and could barely find room to taste the last few dishes.  Just when we thought we were done, more food arrived.  The first course (or round) of dishes was overwhelming.  Six dishes at once was a bit much.  I would have preferred to stagger them a bit.  We could barely fit it all on our table.  But I did enjoy everything, especially the goat cheese with a cherry-fig something or other.  

The service was good.  Our waiter was enthusiastic and knowledgeable but not overbearing.  He answered questions and chatted about the dishes.

To drink, we ordered a pitcher of sangria.  It was good but would probably be better suited to a hot day.

When going here be ready to unleash your inner carnivore. Vegetarians beware! Especially if you are sensitive to seeing large pieces of often rare meat on skewers. 

 The waiter service was excellent. Our waiter was very friendly & well spoken, our glasses were never more than half empty for over 30 seconds and he exchanged any plates which became too messy. The meats were all well cooked (depending on how you like your meat cooked but they are more then happy to bring you any type or prep of meat you wanted.) The fillet mignon was wonderful, by far the favorite of our group. I was impressed with the quality of the salad bar as well. The presentation is nice and it was constantly being restocked with fresh ingredients. 

One small complaint on the decor though. The decor is beautiful with impressive walls full of wine.
Food was very good as well as the drinks.  The issue was there were 4 of us and we sat upstairs where it was very hard to hold a conversation due to the noise.

The food and service were good and I really like the setting... except for the noise level.  I couldn't hear the person I was dining with so it wasn't the best experience.  It will make me hesitate next time I'm thinking of dropping in for a meal.  

I'll be happy when Philly restaurants get the message that people want to talk during a meal.  Or maybe it's a generational thing and only people over 25 don't want to raise their voices that high.

First time at Cin-Cin.  I called in to make a reservation late on a Friday afternoon for that evening. They could get us in "no problem". Got there at 7PM, and man, was that joint jumpin'! Rooms & decor are very nice, high ceilings - better than I was expecting. They sat our party of 5 after about 10-15 minutes after arrival. Service was immediate, attentive and helpful. I'm not sure I would call the menu French-Asian Fusion, but I would definitely call it delicious Asian. As other reviewers on here have mentioned, much better meals than you'd ever get at a Chinese takeout. There were mixed reviews from our party of 5, but overall I was very pleased with my meal, and as usual, I reached over and sampled some of my wife's appetizer and entree, both were delicious.

Unbelievable loud. We were at a table for four and could only speak to the person directly opposite us. Diagonal conversations weren't possible. Screaming, maybe. My ears were ringing the next day and my voice was hoarse.  Surly and condescending service. Frankly, I don't the guy cared at all.  Food was average. 

Tip for business:  Sound baffles!  Curtains, soft panels, anything!

My wife and I ate at Macaroni's Restaurant on Friday night.  Dinner was at 7 pm, and it was fairly empty.  We were seated right away, even though it filled up shortly after.

Service was prompt and attentive, although the waiter failed to describe my wife's fish dish (Chilean Sea Bass) adequately, since it had clams and a seafood broth, which she has an aversion to.  No problem, the clams went to me, and the seafood broth was not objectionable to her.  She enjoyed the fish.  I had the Linguini Umberto, which contained a medley of shell fish in a light red sauce (I chose red because I was drinking a nice Montalcino d'Abruzzo).  It was a fine dish.

All in all, the service and food were quite good (although very pricey), but the experience was not enjoyable because of the noisiness of the restaurant.

We arrived for supper on a Tuesday evening on time for our reservation; however, we had to wait for ten minutes on the sidewalk to be seated inside. We ended up at a table in a corner. The special cocktails were good as was the service.  My entree of pork belly was well cooked and a generous serving. The complaint I have was the cacophony in the room. I think there was music but it was hard to tell with the din created by the other diners and the ambient noise. It is not pleasant to have to raise one's voice to speak to a dinner partner sitting two feet away at the same table and it detracts substantially from the dining experience. At least eliminate the music--no one can hear it anyway.
This is a fun restaurant. The food is delicious and the servers are very pleasant and helpful. The only downside is that it gets really loud.

The food is very good- that is not the problem. But if part of dining out is the company and conversation of those you are with, forget it.  The noise level on this Saturday night was deffining.  Everyone in there was nearly screaming, certainly shouting, and one table near us were actually screaming as they told their story to each other.  

One problem might be the BYOB which means folks bring quite a bit that won't go on the bill, and they drink a lot.  The other problem is we called and made a reservation but that didn't matter. We still waited 45 minutes for our table and a party of two who the host knew, who had no reservation, we're seated in a matter of minutes.

Once we were seated it took one hour before our entrees arrived. The salads that came before that we're good, but not enough to hold the wait and make up for the roar of noise in that tiny space.
Excellent food, nice staff, good facility. But the music is so loud, it seems designed to drive customers away.

Service: attentive, friendly, helpful
Atmosphere: cool, relaxed
Drinks: nice menu of beer and other things drinkable.  Tried 3 different beers and enjoyed them all.
The snacks: wings were good and not overdone as is often the case with wings. Crab cake sandwich was tasty and filling with a good crust and a decently thick filling, bread roll was fresh.  Sandwich and wing veggies (onion, lettuce, tomato, celery, carrot) all freshly cut, I.e. none of that stuff cut up earlier and sitting around which is something a lot of places do.  Food Presentation, for what it was, was also ok (I.e. food was not just thrown on the plate).

All in all: a cool meeting place with a good vibe and friendly people working there. I went for dinner/snacks/a couple of drinks and most people seemed not to be eating and just having drinks.

Great lunch place! The decor is adorable and fun. We were sat upstairs on the balcony overlooking the main eating area, but the view was basically greenery from large "trees".  There was cozy fireplace upstairs (wonderful in this rainy spring day). Our waitress greeted us and took our order and made recommendations. She checked back to let us know the coffee would be a couple of minutes as she was making a fresh pot. My companion and I both ordered burgers with the upcharge sweet potato fries. They are crispy on the outside and tender on the outside with just the right amount of salt. These are highly addictive!!
I got the Big Blue Burger and added mushrooms to the blue cheese and bacon burger. It was chargrilled to perfection. I enjoyed it completely. My companion got the guacamole and bacon burger and added grilled onion and the sweet potato fries.

Very good food. Very cool restaurant, but it was very noisy. If you need a quiet conversation, this is not a restaurant for you, but if you want to have fun, then the place is definitely for you, I recommend.

I dined here with a co-worker tonight and was impressed by the food. My first impression upon walking in was that the atmosphere was hip and stylish. We were sat in the back window where it was cozy and dimly lit. My cornbread was warm with rich flavor and pulled apart so easily. For my main course I got the grilled market fish which was a fish I've never heard of, but I gave it a chance based on the waitress' description. It came out covered in greens and was seasoned very nicely. The cauliflower was charred with a touch of paprika on top which was a nice side to accompany the white fish. Overall it was an enjoyable night, but I must admit that service was slow. It wasn't even close to packed and took quite some time to get our orders in, as well as the check. The bathroom was also on the second floor which is a little bit inconvenient.

This restaurant is very popular. Plenty of people were waiting for tables around the front desk. Because of our reservation, we entered directly into the restaurant. It's so important on weekends. The food is good, but the environment is too noisy. We don't like talking loudly.
Like most Stephen Starr restaurants (especially the older ones), it is quite noisy and difficult to have a conversation when crowded.

The food here is wonderful.
The restaurant itself is very small.
If you are planning to have a conversation over dinner, this is not your place. It can get very loud in there and the tabels are very close together.
The food is great though - so it's worth the experience.

Holy shit this place get's wayyy too loud. If the inside is even close to full don't bother. You probably won't be able to hear a word your friends are saying unless they yell. From now on I will only eat inside if it is close to empty. Either stop playing music that will make people talk louder or get some sound absorbent materials in place. Looking at other reviews I'm not the only one that has been put off by this issue...

PS- Get the hell off my lawn!!

The food was good. Decor, service and location were excellent.  

The sound level was deafening, however. 95 decibels constant (equivalent to a jackhammer at 50' or a subway train at 200') with occasional forays into 100 decibels (snowmobile, motorcycle - a level at which sustained exposure may result in hearing loss). Conversation was impossible.

I would return to this restaurant only if serious sound deadening measures were taken.

I have no issue with a sports bar atmosphere on one side of the restaurant, and music on the other, but the staff had the music SO loud in this place that it was quite literally hard to have a conversation. This is no exaggeration!  In my opinion, it is quite unprofessional to have several large screen TVs on for the patrons, with NO TV sound and NO closed-captioning to make up for loud music, and to be quite frank, the music was  the type you might hear in a nightclub, and just as loud (not kidding).  This type of music is not for relaxing and enjoying a game on TV at the bar, nor is it appropriate for those who want to have dinner with their families. It was very loud dance music, and I saw nobody dancing or even appearing to be interested in the music.

Not coming back until they turn down the horrible "music." I think the food and service were excellent but I could not hear the conversation nor properly digest. Please get rid of the unnecessary noise!

Good food, WAY TOO LOUD ATMOSPHERE.

I don't know who is in charge of the music but they should be fired or better yet be forced to get a bad tattoo. (Just kidding about the tattoo, most of the staff already have really bad tattoos.)

In all seriousness take some earplugs.This was the first time I left a restaurant with my ears ringing.

Some of the items on the menu are okay, but my overall experiences have never been stellar. First off, the place is SO LOUD! They should really invest in some sound-deafening panels on the walls and ceiling. I can barely hear the person sitting next to me and have to shout if there is a decent crowd. The awful acoustics completely ruin any chill experience you were trying to have. On another occasion, I had awful service from one of the downstairs bartenders. I was there to attend a musical event upstairs and wanted to get a beer at the downstairs bar. After waiting patiently for 5 minutes, I wasn't even acknowledged by the bartender. When I leaned in to say something, I was met with a "hold on, I have other guests..I'll get to you when I can". I just ended up going to the upstairs bar, which didn't have as much of a selection, but at least the bartender was fairly responsive.

I've eaten there several times. While the food is always super-tasty and delicious, the service is inconsistent.  The larger the group the harder things seem to be for them to handle.

The last time we went with a group of 12 and they escorted us upstairs - we thought we were going to our table but they just took us to the upstairs bar area with really no explanation.  We were clearly in the way of the servers dodging them as there is little to no walking room. Just thought it could have been handled better.  Across the board the food was great as were the adult beverages. Actually I don't think I've ever heard anyone I was with say they did not like the food. 

The place is very noisy so if you like quiet dinners you may not want to eat here. If you can handle that then I would definitely recommend this place.

Wow !  Having looked at the 4 and 5 star ratings, I had to check this place out.
Arrived ~ 5:30, Friday for a nice quiet, leisurely dinner.  Did we ever go to the wrong place. The bar area was packed, that's a good sign. Tables/food area, not so much. That's fine.  The problem was the music was playing at an ungodly, deafening sound.  Realized then that everyone at the bar was screaming at the top of their lungs to be heard by the person next to them.  We turned around and left.

If you're looking for a quiet, relaxing place for an enjoyable dinner, this is not the place.  If you're looking to have your eardrums pierced, go right in.

When you traverse around the inconveniently placed pole at the front entrance, you enter a restaurant where the music plays softly, but you still hear it, and your conversation isn't drowned out by the conversations of other diners, even when they are 2-3 feet away. Not to mention the open kitchen smack dab in the seating area isn't noisy either. I hate a restaurant that is too loud or painfully quiet, and this place was just right. Seriously, I salute the person responsible for your acoustics. The menu is always changing, but I would say if you ever see the Tasmanian Sea Trout on the menu, do not hesitate to order it because it was the smoothest, tastiest fish I have ever had. 

I will definitely be coming back here, it is worth every cent paid. However, I'd say to fully appreciate a place like this, you should reserve it for very special occasions.

I am a steak fan.  I love it.  I look forward to every steak dinner.  Which is why, when I found myself in Philadelphia for a few days for work, I had to check out several of the steak establishments.  After seeing the photos of this place, I had to check it out.

A couple main points.  1.  This is a very large place - very ornate, two stories, with a huge wine tower.  2.  It was LOUD.  Before I arrived, I was expecting something somewhat quaint and quiet for our party of four.  We walked in and it was so loud you had to yell into your neighbors ear.  It wasn't quite as loud as a nightclub, but it was close.  This was partially due to the live music downstairs, but even upstairs, the acoustics of the space are such that sound bounces off all the walls, and it is nearly deafening.

We sat at a booth and our waiter was there immediately.  Ordered drinks and they arrived quickly.
I love this place. The food is always great; there's ample seating with tables; and the tea selection is amazing! Music is never too loud and people tend to be very quiet which is great for working.

The waitstaff was friendly, helpful and efficient on a busy Friday night. 

Only downside - Poor acoustics and way too noisy for talking. 

Certainly come for happy hour and a zillion tequila options. Think twice if you want a romantic evening in a quiet corner.  This is not that place.

To sum up our experience: Overpriced, Over-salted, Overrated

Low Points:
- Too noisy!  We had advance reservations for a party of 10 and had requested a quiet table in the outer area away from the bar .  We were seated inside against the wall right across from the bar.  We asked for an alternative and were told there were none, even though it was early and there were plenty of open tables in the area we wanted.  The end result is that we were not all able to converse with each other.
- Many dishes we had that night we so over-salted that we neither enjoyed them nor continued eating them.  It was not just one or two people, eventually, the whole table was talking about it.  Examples: herb crusted halibut with baby beets and Swiss chard... the beets and chard were inedible.  
- We were not told that the steak that was listed as "$50 for two" was actually $50 per person.

Great food, great service, and a pretty restaurant. What could go wrong? For some reason, the restaurant had exact lighting and music they play when they turn up the lights at the end of the night in a bar when they're trying to get you go home. It's hard to describe, but it really ruined the atmosphere for my friend and I who were trying to have a quiet dinner. It was more like eating in a cafeteria than a nice restaurant.

This place is a pub (well more on that in a sec.) but they have a ton of food business and even a steak shop, that was hopping late into the night, attached. BUT THEY WERE BLARING THE MUSIC LIKE IT WAS SOME SOUTH ST. MEAT MARKET! I can't stress enough, it wasn't just loud, but insanely loud! Everyone was having to yell at each other and read lips, including servers to customers. We complained and for a hot minute the guy turned it down, but 20 minutes later his jam came on and up it went. Also, the A/C seemed to be an issue with definite pockets of oven like heat zones that are battled by near arctic blasts over other areas, namely our table. As best as I could tell the music and a/c are not evenly dispersed throughout the place so one area is hot and quiet and the other is cold and loud, no middle ground. This will not stop me from going back, the crabs where that good.
Quiet, comfortable and all of the food was absolutely delicious. Friendly waitress. Lighting could be a less bright.

Let me start with I've been to this place before and other across the country and have nothing but good experiences.  But tonight was completely different. 

It began at check in. I explained I needed a table that was on the quiet side as my associate has hearing issues but I guess they didn't hear me!  They placed us on a table on a corner surrounded by other large tables filled with load people.  So the atmosphere was not very good at all! 

The waiter never introduced himself by name as all he wanted to do was tell us the specials.  We were to eat and go back to hotel so my associate knew what he wanted.  We each ordered our main and he asked for a soup and I and salad. My salad came out rather quickly but I waited for his soup to eat.  We had to finally remind our waiter about the soup after waiting about 15 minutes!!! He came right back with the soup and we both began to eat.

The music is so quiet sometimes that you can barely hear it so I feel like other tables can hear my conversations, because I can hear theirs. I still go there so there is no problem big enough that it has stopped me from coming back. They defiantly need to work their service though.

I'll tell why I am not awarding a 5 star review. THE NOISE. THE DIN.

First, by all means-make a reservation and eat here. Do it repeatedly. Do not, however, plan an intimate evening with a loved one, a business dinner or any other type of dining occasion that necessitates ongoing conversation that all parties can actually hear. This is a very small, narrow, converted row house that seats maybe 30 people. The poor acoustics will make you want to get take out, but eat in, eat fast (just kidding) and order enough so you'll have leftovers for the quiet of your home.

Of course, the food is so delicious and delightful, once you start, you don't want to eat fast. You want to savor every mouthful, every morsel and then lick the serving vessel along with your utensils.

I was here with a group. We had a special tasting menu though all the dishes we ate are all on the regular menu.

Not the best place to go.  It's rather loud and the food is ok.  What really got me was my request, upon booking AND arrival (with 70% of the restaurant clear) for a cozy, quiet table.  I found the hostess a bit snarky but ok and we were seated next the kitchen entrance.  We asked to move but it seemed more a chore than doable.  I swear 150+ people walked behind me.  Server was good, drinks, meh.  Won't go back.  Was really hoping for a great experience but was let down.  Way over priced too.  Three adults and a child for $200 less tip.

Came here in the beginning of September with my girl for a date night, we ordered off the pre fixe menu and let me tell you EVERYTHING was delicious. Service was above and beyond friendly, ambiance was good just a bit loud for me but understandable because it's a small place. For people with hearing impairments the sound in a place can really make a difference. All I suggest is maybe some sound proof paneling to hang from the ceiling to quiet it down a bit and it would be amazing!

The taste was flavorful but a bit tough and hard to chew.  Loved the refried beans.. Plain old white rice with cilantro, keep that away. Or at least give me enough to fill me up.  Sheesh,  a spoonful? Sweet Lord.. That wasn't enough to quiet that howling dog a few tables over.. 

At $17, I'd like more food.. Seriously, I was still hungry after leaving.  

Overall,  would I come back? Probably. For happy hour or any time they have a special. I don't think they serve your money's worth here.  And on any other day, pair bad parking with overpriced food and drinks, you'll probably be pissed .

We all had our bills handed to us, most with credit cards, and one of the members of our party..who had driven all day and was rightfully exhausted and downed a few beers got a little loud for a minute.  He wasn't cursing, or being rude, just screamed out "BOOM!" and at that point our waiter, who was helping the only other 2 customers in the restuarant at that moment, turned around and scolded him as if he was a child. It wasn't a polite "can you please quiet down?" It was something like "will you please stop that, it is obnixous like really." We all froze for a minute in disbelief especially since we were all in the process of writing our tips.  I am all for asking a loud crew of people to please quiet down, but not in a way that makes people feel like children.

The ambience was relaxing and peaceful for Center City. It's located on a quiet street. The sidewalk where the outdoor tables sit is pretty large, so you don't feel crammed against the restaurant or too close to people walking by. Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience for our party of four!
I really like the ambiance of this place, I frequent after a day at work when I want good coffee, a few quiet people around me, good vibes and easy seating. It's quiet but inviting.

Great food in a peaceful and relaxing atmosphere. The only drawback is short and abrupt phone manners (by a man, name unknown) when placing take out orders. Some niceties would be appreciated from customers spending their money at your restaurant rather than hundreds of other options in the immediate area... Rather than rushing people off of the phone just to get to the next call.

We made a 7:00p Tuesday night reservation recently and were seated promptly upon our arrival.  Initially the restaurant was quiet but by 7:45 the place was packed. Our party of three enjoyed their food.  We shared a couple of apps: shrimp dumplings were excellent and our lettuce wraps were just ok.  Entrees: Pork with peanut sauce, Drunken Noodles with Shrimp and Scallops with Spinach were all excellent.  The restaurant has an interesting variety of Thai and Fusion entrees.  As the restaurant filled up the noise level was high but bearable (restaurant is relatively small).  BYOB is nice and it is a very good restaurant that and we will definitely be back.  If you want intimate dining with a quiet atmosphere, this is not the place.  If you want excellent food and are not concerned with a little noise, then this place is for you.

Atmosphere is wonderful, can be loud or quiet. The ambiance is so worth a lunch or dinner at this place! I had a nice little quiet area on the upper floor. The food and drink options are really diverse including interesting soft drinks. Customer service was excellent. I had the rabbit pie and it was quite good. I also had a salad which was good but not filled with as many items as I would have liked.

I always take my friends out to this restaurant whenever my friends visit me. 
It's really beautiful inside and it's quiet so that I can talk to friends. 
If you have a first date, take a woman out to here. They will love it. 

pros
- Awesome service. 
- Quiet and nice environment
- Great location
- Variety of wine collections

cons
- Food is good but it won't surprise you too much. I would love to go back and try the sunday brunch since I see a lot of reviews on them. I had only been here during lunch and dinner.

Disorganized staffing and seating and highly prejudiced. If I could give them zero, then I would. The staff/management do not treat you respectively and often snap at you just because they want to. My sister was standing near the bar because there was no room and a server wanted to get by and the server screeched "EXCUSE ME" at her. 

There was a family there who were being completely disrespectful toward us and sent an 8 year old child to tell us to quiet down in a public space (literally it's a restaurant and bar). We weren't being any louder than any other table as everyone was speaking loudly in the establishment. Every other table had people talking, drinking and enjoying a good time but they chose a table of Asian people to come tell us to quiet down. Management completely failed at being unbiased and poorly handled the situation.

This was one of the best meals I had during the 4 years I went to school in Philly.  I saved it for my senior year, and it was well worth the wait.  The service was impeccable, and the food itself was amazing.  I was temporarily overwhelmed by the variety and couldn't decide if I wanted to take the sweet or savory brunch route.  Luckily the buffet setup allows you to do a little of both.

The place was a little more quiet and formal than I'm usually comfortable with, but who cares when you have such a great brunch spread before you?

I've only been here for brunch but it is one of my go-to places to eat on a weekend. I've had several of their brunch meals but always with a side of sausage. I don't normally order a side of sausage but it is that good. Recently I had their 9-grain pancakes with bananas. I was pleasantly surprised when I received the pancakes and the bananas were cooked into the pancake - score! Everything I've ever gotten there is fresh and tasty. I really enjoy the bread basket that includes cornbread, rye, and some other yummy slices and jelly. Depending on who is paying I would advise getting a mimosa. I word it that way because I think they are too expensive but very tasty. 

Overall I love this place. I can always expect fresh and tasty food. I also can always expect a wait (on the weekends for brunch). I've found that if you arrive at 10:45 or earlier you don't have too long of a wait.

I like this little joint for their delicious coffee and amazing service, but I hate that they allow about 15-20 people in this very small space. It's definitely beyond full capacity because all the tables are full and people waiting in line inside from the bathroom area to the other side of the entrance. It's SCARY because that's definitely putting people in danger.

I used to love coming here for date night, but now it feels like they overbook shows and understaff for service. I came in here tonight with my husband and we got seated at a small shared table with another couple, with not enough space for food and drinks so that I had to hold my drink on my lap the whole time. On top of that, it felt like we were intruding on the other couple's date because I was sitting closer to them than my husband.  When we asked to be moved to another table, we were told that they were sold out and didn't have any other tables available (even though there were many visible since we arrived early).
