I would definitely recommend people to visit them and have a great meal.

Ordered Andy's through Caviar - delivery was quick and everything was hot. We got a half original/traditional and a half sweet chili for three people. Chicken pieces seemed on the small side, but we had plenty of food. Chicken was fine - crisp, pretty moist. But nothing to write home about. Overall we liked the original better than the sweet chili. But honestly probably won't return - would rather hit Southgate for their KFC next time a Korean fried chicken urge hits. 

The two stars is really for the sides. Onion rings were fine, as were fries (if a bit grease-laden). But the slaw and macaroni salad were horrible - I can make better slaw, and the macaroni salad was sweet (???). Also, SMALL portions for $3.50. Total bill (with delivery and tip) was close to $50 for a dinner that was not memorable at all.

Had lunch on the upper level. Thought the restaurant would be more like the old Shanks on 10th Street - crazy counter service, huge portions. It was a little to foofy - go the counter, they give you a number and the staff brings you this little sandwich on this huge tray. The chicken parm sandwich was good but for 8.50$.... and on a round roll?...  and the chicken milanese sandwich was very good. However very small portions and very overpriced. Nothing spectacular. Won't really hurry back.

Very impressive! Nothing was less than excellent when a family of 4 all had the $48 prix fixe menu. One from each category was enough to satisfy (and fill) the appetites of everyone. Warrants an impressive, meaningful bottle of wine, too.

So many restaurants these days provide "tapas", i.e., tiny portions where everyone looks to others for the last serving. This place is large portions of solidly good, interestingly presented, well-sauced memorable creations, including the daily fish offering. No "molecular" cuisine; no "way too many ingredients to really work" dishes. Just a few well-chosen ingredients in each course that harmonize into a satisfying whole dish.

As these things go, the prix fixe menu is a real deal, too. Even the made-on-premises gelatos were memorable. 

This is the "whole deal": good and inspired from start to finish. Great pasta dishes. Interesting appetizers.

I love bourbon based drinks and this did not disappoint! It was delicious - - I would happily ask for it again. It seemed that it was not well known to staff, and it did not appear on the menu, but they managed to surprise me with a lovely drink. 

This is the kind of place that is good to have in one's back pocket but I wouldn't go far out of my way to go....Amada feels like a more exciting indulgence, admittably. I paid for dinner for two and it cost me at least $100 for a satisfying meal, despite the small portions. I didn't feel i needed huge portions. All my wine choices were quite nice as well. 

Incidentally, I did have lunch there recently. I had a glass of sparkling wine and the hearts salad, which was satisfying enough but probably not worth the price. It was ok. The service, though, kind of made it feel worth dropping in for lunch!

A major thing that bothered me was that the POS station is out in the open, and the servers and a seating hostess(?) was kind of loitering about. It's very unprofessional and weird for the observing guests to see them just chit-chat and casually lean around.  

This place has the potential to be upscale casual dining, but little details revealed a lot of their flaws that I can't say that I'm a fan of this place. 

But the large portions are great for sharing with a group of people!

A lot of places, especially Italian places, will give you huge portions, leaving you feeling way too full after your meal. So I was very happy that this place gave you normal-sized dishes that leave you satisfied but not bursting. I really wish more places did this.

We're so happy we had the random opportunity to check this place out!

I can't say enough good things about our visit to Giuseppe & Sons. We went for the first time last night during Restaurant Week. We have been going to Center City Restaurant week for many years and for the most part have never had a bad meal...but a lot of places provide smaller portions and a limited menu during the promotional pricing time. Not the case for this restaurant. The courses are served family style and include four courses. By the time the main course came out, we were already full. So first and foremost I would highly recommend trying for Restaurant week...but we will be back to try some of the other entrees outside of this. We had beef carpaccio and meatballs for our appetizer/salad course. Both were very tasty and good portion size. Ricotta tortelloni and Rigatoni alla vodka for the pasta course - not huge portions but both were very filling and just enough.

Good portion sizes all around.

Atmosphere 3.5/5: There were a few other customers in for an early dinner, but otherwise the place was next to empty. Clean, well-kept but slightly cold (temperature) and not particularly decorated or done up in any way. The lack of decor did leave the impression that their focus was only on the food, not on the ambiance.

Service: 3.5/5: We had minimal interaction with our server aside from ordering. The meal largely felt like a business transaction rather than a dining experience. We asked if there was tea or hot water (since it was cold out) and after a round, were told that the kitchen was out. As soon as we were finished, the general vibe was to urge us to pay and leave. 

Overall, decent food and good portion sizes. Large selection of menu items. But food, service and atmosphere lacked the finesse to go from good to great.

The tl;dr version of this summary is MEH.

So, if you browse my profile, you'd quickly find out my thing is cheap, huge portions, with compassion for sacrificed quality and service to get those cheap, huge portions.  I should have been a pig in shit at Q.T., then.  A fancy sandwich?  For less than five dollars?  For 4.95$ to be exact?

Problem is, some things you want done right and can get done right for even cheaper (South Philly Viet food, be gentle with my heart).

I ordered a #7, which is a plain pork banh mi (and they come with pate, fyi).  The meat was actually pretty good: very fatty, smoky.  I personally liked the roll, which was a little crunchier than some others I've had.  

What SANK this sandwich for me was the vegetables.  There weren't really enough of them, for starters, and they were totally dry.

I ordered catering from Pita Chip for about 20 people. The manager in charge of catering was incredibly helpful in putting an order together for me. There was plenty of food, and they were able to handle all of our dietary restrictions. 

The food itself was fantastic. We had chicken shawarma and falafel, both of which were delicious, as were the assorted sauces that they gave us with our food. And of course, the hummus was great. They also gave us rice, salads and pita (again, plenty of food!) I hope I can stop by and order a plate some time soon!

Off the beaten path, low key, great Philly Cheesesteak at Saad's in West Philly. The restaurant is tucked away in West Phila and there is only street parking. Also, be prepared that it is cash only up to $30. There is an  ATM for convenience in the back of the location for a $1 fee.  All drinks are bottled products but there is a great variety.

The food is very good. Enjoyed a cheesesteak with fried onions. Steaks traditionally come with mayo and ketchup which I am high on both for a Philly steak. The sandwich is a great size, is delicious and sits perfectly on a slightly toasted roll that does a great job to keep all the steak kept inside of the roll. 

Also tried a chicken shish tawook sandwich which was delicious. It is like a halal cart platter wrapped in a pita. Also available on a long roll.

The interior is dated and the seating gives off an '80s feel but the staff is very helpfu

It was always packed on the Sunday mornings we'd tried to come here for brunch, so we took advantage of our Monday-after-Thanksgiving off to come by for a nice leisurely meal. As we perused the menu and enjoyed the kitsch on the wall, a woman on her way out stopped by our table to warn us of the portion sizes. We laughed and thanked her, but figured it was nothing we couldn't handle. I even asked the waitress how large the french toast serving was, and six half slices didn't sound so bad. 

Do not take this warning lightly! Holy moly these portions are huge! Excessively so! Bring a small troupe to dine with you and only order a few things big! The prices are a bit steep, but that's because no lone person should be able to eat that much food in one sitting =P

So I read Kevin C's assessment of Fiesta Pizza's pasta and I ordered the manicotti and it wasn't bad. Usually pasta from pizza places is kind of mushy, but the manicotti was not mushy, large portioned and a good value. It's not any kind of pasta you might get in South Philly, but it's tasty/cheap.

I also enjoy the mini strombolies--another great value for the price--just massive.

This place has potential but one major problem needs to be fixed. They give you the tiniest portion of food I've ever been given at a restaurant but the price tag makes you say "where's the rest of my food"!!!! No exaggeration everyone at our table looked astonished at the tiny portion size.

I ordered cuba libre chicharrones which is supposed to be a platter of grilled steak, chicken sausage and tostones. I was given two of the smallest pieces of each of the meats described above and 1 just 1 lonely toston. The dish was very tasty and full of flavor. It's just hard to get over the portion size.

Next I got the vaca frita this is supposed to shredded flank steak with rice, beans, and sweet plantains. I almost felt insulted when I looked at the amount of food I was given for the $25 price tag on this dish. The rice and the beans came in these two tiny bowls.

I loved the vibe here but the portions are pretty small and you definitely need to order a lot of small plates to share if you're feeling anywhere above semi-hungry.

Loved the wings and would order that again!
Awesome food! Portions could be a little bigger...but still REALLY good!

View was great, such a nice breeze on deck and food tasted wonderful. Portions, however, were sad. We were so excited to try the restaurant and figured we would come for restaurant week but the portion sizes were so variable and some so pathetic. One of our guests got the tuna tartar app and it was probably one bite of food. My boyfriend who has a large appetite got the rainbow trout which he probably could have finished in three bites, it was embarrassing! We had to go get him something to eat after our expensive meal out.

An update on my previous review! COVID-19 has rocked the city but this place definitely comes through! Their tables are situated outside and they are actually shaded due to the building! So when we got there at 6:30 on a Thursday night, it was cool and breezy and Perfect.

The staff are friendly and hope you weren't waiting for the table and sitting down. The tables are numbered so it's easy to identify. And if you wear your mask you can certainly go inside and use the restroom. Other than that, no one enters. Besides the staff

The food here is delicious and a small bit on the pricey side but it's worth it for the location, scenery, and atmosphere.

We fancy the caterpillar bread, the cheesesteak bao, the Dan Dan noodles, and the Koji beef. 
They also told us the pork soup dumplings, even though they weren't on the menu, were an option so of course we got those too!
Our food didn't get to our table for over an hour. The dishes were mediocre. The portions were very small. Don't waste your time.
Great taste, portions were huge, food was till hot when it received it....no complaints here

Bai Wei, previously Sakura popped up as one of the RESTAURANT WEEK options this winter. Bai Wei's restaurant week menu offered three courses plus dessert but we decided to order a la carte. The appetizers - pork soup dumplings, scallion pancakes, chicken in diced red pepper, the typical Chinese staples were decent, nothing out of the ordinary but the entrees truly sets them apart from other Chinatown haunts. With a terrific range of options, we got to experience a great range of Chinese food from Shanghai to Sichuan and more. 

The fish filet with peppercorn was one of the best fish dishes I've had in a while. The smelly pot with chicken and sichuan sauce scores high on presentation and taste.  The dish has 'smelly' tofu, hence the name. You can choose to order this with less spicy sauces if you have a low tolerance for spice. The Japanese tofu and shrimp is another standout.

This place is way overpriced and definitely lacking in their portions sizes for the prices of their entrees. The step down dining, is something I like. It's a slightly dark place. The lighting from the small track lights above do just enough illumination. It reminds me of a reformed wine cellar. The booths are tall, yet you sit at ground level. All around you are those scientific artist renderings of various species of seafood. Be that as it may, I wasn't impressed. Where as with Lacroix, I was treated to something special. This was kind of normal, average. I digress. I really love their complementary biscuit, served with sweet butter cream. More please! For our appetizer we had the small order of Muscles in garlic butter juice. I love seafood and Muscles especially. There was enough for the both of us and it came with a nice size of (Sourdough?) garlic bread.

I was excited to share Stateside with out of town guests last night. I noticed the place wasn't packed which surprised me on a Friday night. After being seated, I realized that the menu was new. The waitress explained that there was a new chef and the current menu was 1/2 of what it eventually will be. There were about 10 items on the menu. The waitress said the items were meant to be shared and with a group of 4, we would each get a bite. She wasn't kidding. The portions were so small that we each had only 1 bite of each item. The flavor was good and presentations were nice, but the portions were just too small for the price. Our favorites were the brown butter tagliatelle and the rabbit risotto - we just wanted more. We're no strangers to shared plates or haute cuisine, but the small portion sizes were a but out of hand.

Beautifully designed restaurant, friendly staff and overall great food! We had one main issue: Since all the plates are "made to share," we asked about sizing, etc. I felt that our server recommended that we order way more plates that we really needed. (We could have easily been perfectly fine with three fewer dishes). On the positive side, we had a lot of leftovers, but we really didn't need all that food. I would definitely return, but will be more aware of the plate sizes next time.

You can't go wrong! The food you get is sooo good and flavorful. There isn't anything on the menu that I haven't tried and haven't liked. What I also love is the portion size; I'm a light eater so there have is enough for my daughter and leftover  :D

Good food but the portions are tiny. One thing about the other reviews is the portion size is a very small component. So as my boyfriend and I walked in a couple was coming out and warned us not to go there because the portions were so small. I didn't listen and we went in. It's true the portions are small. It's not going to be Maine lobster. But I did enjoy my four bites of food. This sandwich was less than the size of my hand. If I wasn't so hungry we'd have kept walking. 

In the end it's a snack. I had a really great snack in Philly one time.

The portions are a lot bigger than they look. My boyfriend and I went (he's a very picky eater), and we didn't think it would be enough. We both ended up getting two meals out of our bowls. Phenomenal!
Nothing special. most dishes were above average but the portions were way too small. this place would be wonderful if they gave more food. PERIOD.

This is a scam of a restaurant.  The aesthetics are nice but there are two very atrcious issues with this place

1) The portions are unfathomably small.  A $13 meal gets you three tiny pieces of chicken and enough rice to fit on one fork.  This is my second time coming here and my last.  Both times they fed me as if my stomach was the size of a dime.

2) They have windows looking into the bathrooms?  Like being watched while you pee?  Come here.


Additionally, the manager refused to take the food back and made us pay even though we did not touch the food.  Do not come here.
Experience was great. One dish was a little too salty, but everything else was fantastic. I really enjoy the style of serving the dishes with larger portions that are intended to be shared.

The ambiance is great.   The portions are enormous for the price,  and the preparation was faultless.   Weirdly  ... And I don't think I've ever had to mention this before  ... The biggest problem was that the tables aren't big enough for the size of plates they serve.   By the time everything was on the table  ... And we only ordered one entree and two smaller dishes  (spicy creamy cucumbers and dan dan noodles) ... We were practically balancing food on our laps.  It detracted from an otherwise nice experience.

Food is absolutely delicious! I came in on sunday with my girlfriend and we looked around and noticed that the serving size is huge! I ended only ordering one main dish and one side to share and it was just enough. The food is flavorful and the service is very professional. I can't wait to come back to try their other dishes!

Service was terrific, and the food was excellent. It's easy to over feed yourself, so start slow.  You can order more as you go.

My one gripe is that the portions are slightly too big for one  person.  That makes them good for sharing, but only if other people want what you are eating.  Salads and flatbreads are way too big for one person to have as part of a multi tapas meal. 

Granted, having too much food is not a horrible problem...
Portion sizes are huge so consider sharing. Every plate that came out looked wonderful. We had a great experience with the wait staff and brunch

I went to Vernick with my boyfriend last week. I loved the ambiance and all the waiters were really nice. The owner even came over and chatted with us for a bit.

My biggest complaint: the portions are SO SMALL. I know us Americans need to tone down portions, but this restaurant has taken it to an absurd level. For instance, we paid $15 for an appetizer of mozarella and herbs. It was literally three tiny pieces of cheese with some oil and herbs. Granted, it tasted great, but the size was made for a baby. It was a joke to try to split it with my boyfriend, as we both can really put away food.

By the end, our bill was pretty large - almost $100 including drinks - and I was still very hungry. When I got home, I had a whole bunch of cereal. Overall, I wouldn't recommend Vernick for anyone looking for a meal.

Absolutely loved Double Knot! Took my boyfriend here for an anniversary dinner, and fell in love with the space, atmosphere, food, and service. When you first enter, the space is beautifully designed as an elegant coffee/ cocktail space. We were taken all the way through and down a dark staircase into an entirely different world that is the robatayaki/ sit-down sushi space below. Its dim lighting and incredible decor creates an incredible atmosphere that allows you to have an intimate and unique dining experience. Our servers were incredibly friendly, and very helpful in recommending menu items that would best suit us. 

The cocktail menu is very innovative, and the Monkey's Fist that we tried was both delicious and perfectly balanced. Plates are brought out as they are made, and served family style, which contributes to the tasting experience and pacing of flavors.
Was the food good? Amazing. So good. I'm skinny and don't eat diner size portions however the portion size was inadequate to get even remotely full. Oh well. You just gotta keep ordering I guess ;)

I was here once for restaurant week.  The service was wonderful and for that, I would give 5 stars.  The problem I had was the portion size of the food.  There were 5 of us dining and everyone ordered the prime rib.  The salad was good, the creme brûlée for dessert was also good, and the prime rib was delicious!  However, the prime rib was really thin.  I didn't realize how much smaller our table's portion was until we saw a prime rib be delivered to a nearby table that was at least twice, maybe even three times the size of ours.  On top of that, we were given one tiny dish of mashed potatoes and a tiny dish of green beans to share.  Other tables with only 2 people got the same amount of sides, which left each of us with about a little dollop of potatoes each and a few green beans.
This place is great. I wish their food portions were a little bit bigger but they are still really good. Worth your time and money.

Came here since we saw a lot of good reviews. Nice place and service was good. The only problem is the dishes are too big. There was s no way to finish them and a lot of food is wasted.  My wife had the Huevos and potatoes covered the whole bottom of the plate. Sometimes less is more. Most dishes we saw were just to much to the point where it's not appetizing.

A fancy Italian place overlooking Rittenhouse Park....

The service and food here is phenomenal.  I ordered some foie gras ravioli and it was delicious.  However; there were no more than 10 tiny pieces of them.  Execution of flavors are excellent here, but basically everything that was served from appetizers to pasta dishes were incredibly small.  I wished the server told us this before we ordered, I would have probably ordered two entrees.  Besides that, everything else here was great.  House cocktails are amazing....try them all.

Final thoughts:  Portions are tiny and expensive (glad I didn't have to pay).  I think they should be accurately labeled as small plates.  I enjoyed the experience here, but I went home still hungry and made a sammich.

I enjoyed the variety of flavors in the dishes here, but the portions are way too big. I liked the atmosphere, and our server Evan took care of us with charm and wisdom. Very pleasant dining experience. Food for parties of 2-6.

This review is painful to write as I truly don't want to knock restaurants right now & I had such high expectations of Irwin's. But I do feel obligated to give honest feedback for other patrons. 

First, our server was awesome - there as some "rules" laid out on the table in regards to covid (ex: flip menus & put in center when ready to order to minimize interactions w server) but this wasn't really the case. Our server was friendly, attentive, and spent lots of time explaining to menu to us. 

Ambiance - also awesome! Not the restaurants fault at all, but our table was moved inside due to bad weather. While I know a lot of the allure of this restaurant is the view, the indoor area was super cute and well decorated. The weather got better by the end of our meal and they let us finish our drinks on the rooftop which was great. 

Food - here's where they lose me!

The food is great, the atmosphere is fun, and the price is not bad at all... Their portion sizes have been cut down over the years but its still too much to eat and you have to take some of it home with you.

I so wanted to love this place. Heard plenty of good things, but it just didn't do it for me. Came in on a Friday around dinner time. We were seated quickly with a reservation at a table by the bar. I ordered a bourbon cocktail, which was pretty tasty but extremely small that it almost felt awkward picking up the glass.

We ordered the seafood mixto, cacio e pepe, and speck & egg pizza. Figured an appetizer, pasta, and main would've been sufficient. We were wrong. While everything tasted good, portions were tiny for the price point. After we ordered, bread came out, portioned by slice based on how many people were at the table... I know some places do this, but it was almost ironic as it set the stage for what was to come for the rest of our meal.

The seafood mixto was served in something smaller than a dip bowl. Again, taste was on point, but portion was just way too small.
Food was fresh and delicious. Portion sizes were very large and delivery was fast! Lots of great options, a must try!

Went to this place on a date and was very impressed. The staff was extremely attentive and the food was very good. The place is a little more causal than Id have liked (they have TVs throughout the restaurant) but beyond that, its a great place to check out. 

Just keep in mind that the portions are very large.

I came here for a graduation dinner and the service and food was top notch and definitely deserving of 5 starts. We had a party of 9 people and they seated us within 15 minutes (we did have a prior reservation). 

We ordered the crab curry, chicken curry, chicken tapioca dumplings, papaya salad, crab stir fry, pork belly stir fry, and eggplant stir fry. This Thai food is so authentic you won't even recognize it from the usual Thai food you get here in Philly. The dishes were just an absolute burst of flavor and also very spicy - not for the weak palates! All of the food is so delicious you really can't go wrong. The dumplings are plated so beautifully, it's a fun dining experience. The curries and stir frys are super flavorful and delicious. The papaya salad was refreshing and also kicks with the spice.

Amazing brunch spot !
Everything in the menu is delicious & the portions are fairly big.

I ordered the stuffed meatball, which was very good and reasonably priced. When I received my meal I realized that the relatively low price was due to the smaller than average portion size. As a small person, It was a satisfying portion for me and I didn't leave overstuffed; However, my friend was still a little hungry at the end of the meal, although he enjoyed his steak. 
The restaurant lighting was very dim, which can be nice and romantic, but in my opinion it was slightly too dark for what I like in a restaurant.
Overall, wonderful experience, food, and service. Only downside is the portion size, but the price makes it worth it.

Came here twice and enjoyed the food both times. My food had a lot of flavor and the portions are pretty big, but manageable. The first time, we had a small party but we were seated next to a larger party where everyone was really loud and drinking. We couldnt hear our own voices. So, just dont bring a large group unless you want to be that loud.

If you wish to dine in a quiet, peaceful environment with prompt service, then Wokano is not the place for you. I would just suck it up and take that trip on down to Chinatown.

I've been to Wokano twice. On the first night, it was late and I was dying for Chinese food. I knew my usual spots in Chinatown were a no-go because they were closed. I drove down Washington Ave and noticed that there was a restaurant with their lights on. Cool. I spun the block to pull into the lot and was relieved to see free, nearly endless parking. My friend and I entered and found it to be pretty noisy, with a large party seated at one of the large round table. There were also small children running around. You just have to walk in and sit there and wait to even get noticed. A waiter quickly gestured us over to sit, luckily away from the large noisy party.

That was some delicious food! I only felt bad about not being able to finish a lot of it. Our table of 7 chose to try the 4-course meal (and we had to have the whole table do it). We were excited to try many things, and by having this many people, we ended up being able to try and share almost every item on the menu. All of them were great!  It got a bit crowded trying to fit the plates on our small table, but we managed. Unfortunately, we just couldn't handle the quantity of food. The portions were too large for us, and by the second course, we were already unable to finish all the plates. We had to ask for them to box some, which they were happy to do. The same thing happened for the third and fourth courses.  At least it made for some delicious leftovers...

Service seemed fine to me, especially considering how crowded it was (completely packed, literally).

Misconduct - the name is bad, but it is a great spot!  This is the go-to place to watch any game.  There are lots of TV's, and always a decent view from wherever you're sitting, even outside!  They set up a small outdoor seating area with a TV!  It's a very friendly atmosphere, and even when it's crowded you can still stand or sit at the bar and see with all those TV's in there.  Lots of fun.

Inside it's kinda charmingly cheesy with the nautical theme, but I like it.  The food is so-so, but the scene is really about going to watch a game and have drinks.  The fries were yummy with chipotle mayo, but over-salted.  I had a special salad with duck, citrus over spring mix...eh.  I know, why would I get duck...at Misconduct Tavern?  It was a little bland and there was way too much fennel seed sprinkled on top.

My friend got the mac n cheese with tomato...which looked dee-lish.
Portions are huge, food is excellent. A must try if you haven't been here. Never disappoints!

Stumbled upon this place when El Vez couldn't take us in for 2 1/2 hours, and was thrilled with the staff, food, and drinks. 

Although the restaurant was packed, the host was very kind about keeping an eye on the bar until seats opened up for us. The decor and ambience were beautiful and fit in perfectly with the farm-food theme: think antique barn: wood planks, squash, and candles.

My boyfriend and I ordered the fig and sheep's milk ricotta appetizer which was a hearty first course that did not fill us up too much. I got the house-made basil lemonade, which was delicious and strong.

For dinner, WOW. 

My boyfriend got the stuffed quail (a special that we hope we can get again) which was out of this world. Perfectly seasoned and served with cannelini beans; also fantastic!

I got the smoked pork tenderloin and potatoes with aoli...just amazing.
Amazing, everything thing they have is well done. Some of the portions can be small, but he food is very satisfying.

I honestly can't say enough great things about the food or the staff here. Our experience was fantastic. We asked our waiter about portion sizes due to being big eaters. I will say; we ended up ordering several meals after our first and eating numerous things on the menu.

The portion sizes are, in my opinion, pretty small. So, if you're "starving", be warned. The lighting where we sat could have used some work, too. We used the light from our phone screens to read the menu.

Aside from those 2 gripes; expect an amazing experience with awesome staff and absolutely delicious food. I will be returning to finish the selection. Once I've done that, I'll be returning even more for my faves and the great staff. 

Also; their meat balls... To die for! Best I've eaten. Dethroned Little Nona's for me.
Great food and wonderful experience! The only issue would be the price compared to portion size-- for the appetizers. The entree portions are generous and worth the price!

All I can say is "yummy-oh-so-good!" The portions are super large...more than enough to have left-overs! I took my Grandson and we still had food left. The customer service was wonderful!  I've told numerous family members and friends, that they have to go experience it for themselves. I'm looking forward to going back real soon!
Overrated and overpriced. Atmosphere and drinks are solid.  Portion sizes are ridiculously small. Had to get real food after

I come here because price is reasonable and the food is decent but can't find myself coming here except when it's my last resort. I can't and the guy in the counter. He's so rude and he was exceptionally rude during my last visit. Even threw in a couple f bombs and was also throwing around customers items.

Great Mexican family restaurant.  We knew it was some place special when we tasted the complimentary chips and salsa.  The salsa verde with a balancing blend of avocado to the nicely acidic  verde veg base made you smile. The red chipotle salsa was smoky goodness with complex and pleasingly hot flavor. 

My wife and I both ordered from the specials blackboard, with my wife having the flautas de pollo and I had the  lamb enchiladas.  Can't say how the flautas tasted as the bride wouldn't share but they certainly looked scrumptious with fresh guacamole, wonderfully creamy beans, yellow rice and a shaved lettuce and 3 large slices of avocado as the garnish.   The lamb enchiladas were beautifully braised lamb cubes in a mild red enchilada sauce that crumbled to the fork.  The same sides came with mine but had full basket of warmed tortillas nicely wrapped in an embroidered linen tea towel.

I was pleasantly surprised by this place, from the outside you might expect a chinese food take out ambiance, but it was anything but.  It was well decorated, and the food was great.  The menu is pretty extensive and they have a lot of interesting rolls, not too mention this place is cheap!  Its a BYOB, they deliver, and take credit cards.  I will go back again!

The food is more than reasonably priced, the selection is huge, and everything that I've tasted has been delicious. 

This little place is a neighborhood gem.

Now what's less than ideal is the face that it's located a few blocks away from a high school that allows its students to leave campus for lunch. I showed up today and in typical high school kid fashion, they were everywhere and caused havoc in this tiny shop- making the lunch breaks if those of us trying to pop in on a work break less than desirable. Be mindful of the time in which you're here to avoid such mess.

At first I was disappointed that Thirsty Soul, a neighborhood bar with a quirky interior and great open mic & quizzo was replaced by a Mexican restaurant. South Philly doesn't exactly have a shortage of great Mexican spots. The menu here, however, is a bit more refined than your average barbacoa taqueria type place without being fussy. It is a great addition to the neighborhood.

We went here for brunch and enjoyed the bottomless mimosas, avocado toast, mixed seafood cruda, and a more classic breakfast plate with eggs and chorizo. Everything was great, but the cruda was highlight of the meal. 

The portions are not super large and are priced appropriately. 3 dishes between 2 people was a large meal, 2 dishes would have been a refreshing brunch before a productive day. After the bottomless mimosas, however, we were not having a productive day anyway!

Mannn this place is awesome I got the teriyaki chicken cheesesteak, damn that Asian fusion is good. 
Friendly, welcoming Vibes as well and I appreciated the token of a free carrot cake

When we first pulled up, we didn't know what we were getting ourselves into. Once we walked in, it was very clean. There were two waitresses there; Theresa and another young girl at the front. The young girl was not too welcoming at first. She did not greet my best friend and I until the manager or owner came out of the kitchen to tell her to do so but he noticed us right on the spot so it wasn't long. It would've been nice if she didn't have to be told to acknowledge us. While seating us, she did not make any eye contact at all. For a whole we thought it had something to do our skin tone. After being seated, Theresa our actual waitress came over to us and had a smile and personality that lit up a room. LOVE HER! She made sure my best friend and I had everything we needed and was well taken care off. She was very personable and I really enjoyed talking to her while being waited on.

do not recommed the buffet.... i would not eat the roast beef for obvious reasons .. the server's outfits r fantastic...if bennigans's adopted delilah's uniforms they prob still be in business......they would not let my gfriend and her friends unless they brought guys which i thought was weird

What happened to this place?  The only reason that I am giving two stars is because it USED TO BE excellent, so I feel bad giving 1 star.  I used to love the sandwiches at Shanks, all of them.  I went here a couple of weeks ago and realized that this was not the same Shanks that stood here last year.  I ordered two sandwiches to split and they were disgusting. The chicken cutlet hoagie-  One little piece of chicken that was so overly fried it was almost black. The chicken italiano- same thing, tiny piece of chicken-- waaaaayy overly fried... and the broccoli rabe- ew!!  So bitter, not garlicky.  I ended up throwing most of it in the trash.
Very very consistent....This food is banging and the portions are huge. Definitely recommend giving this place a try.
Got breakfast delivered and it was VERY good! Ordered again and when I picked it up, the place kinda smelled, bad sign. That order was not good and would not order from there again

I will start out by saying this is a beautiful restaurant.  The gold-toned chandelier lighting and the green-toned bar and intricate tiling in the main dining space creates such a relaxing feel.

The service was welcoming and generous.  We started with hummus, a red pepper appetizer, and their special salad of cucumbers and tomatoes all served with delicious puffed up pita.  Both our friends and we ordered fish.  The bass was delicious but the portion was small . Our friends ordered the sword fish and also thought the portion was small. That said, we were very satisfied as we ordered a lot!  

AND they were wonderful about bringing our friends a dessert to celebrate their anniversary.  

WE WILL be back!!!

I would have really expected better for the price you pay. The menu outside had really good prices so we decieded to eat there, then when we sat down, we found out that those were the lunch prices and it was much more for dinner. The service was really slow and had to ask more than once for water refills for the amount of time we were there. I ordered scallops with risotto & fennel salad. It was ok, but they only gave me 5 scallops and I left without being full. My boyfriend had the Chef's Tasting Menu, which was delicious, but not enough food again. I mean there are decent portions, and small portions, and here they are pretty small.

The Restaurant has rooms that are decorated very authentic. I made reservations on line for 7:30. The place was not that busy. Plenty of empty tables downstairs. Yet the hostess took us upstairs in a side corner room with nothing to see but a plain wall. The table next to this one was empty and was by a window, I asked if we could move to that one and she said yes. Being that the Restaurant was not that busy for a Friday night, I should had known why. The drinks were ok but nothing extraordinary. But the food was disappointing. I ordered the pargo(fish) dish. Portion was small for the price, on top of that,  semi warm, and the taste was not all that. My wife had the lechón. Pretty straight forward, Cuban classic, again Two very small portions, with a yuca paste and coleslaw. Very disappointed with the food experience. The service was very good. The waitress was very nice and consistent.

Came here for brunch buffet ($25 pp) for a birthday, and we were nicely accommodated, even as a party of 10 with 2 children. 

The buffet didn't have much variety, but that also meant everything was made well. Also, items were made in small portions so food was hot and fresh. Brunch ranges from various types of eggs, potatoes, pallella, carving station, and charcuterie. The food itself is placed in the back area where the chefs are cooking, so you can actually see them making the food; more the reason to know nothing shady going on with your meal! 

Unfortunately, small selection + small portions also meant every time I went up to get food, about 50% of the items needed to be refilled. I spent a lot of time standing around and waiting for my food.

I had brunch at Aksum and I've got "good" (okay) news and bad news.

THE GOOD/OKAY NEWS: Pricey, small portions of uneven food, ranging between passable to good.

THE BAD NEWS: Service is a lot worse than the food.

THE FOOD is not great & fails to justify the prices or the small portions.

1. Salmon crepes were okay, but way too much syrup was drizzled over the plate, so that the crepes were swimming in syrup & much too sweet.  Since it was all over the plate, I couldn't really avoid the syrup while eating the crepe.  Salmon inside was flavourful but overcooked.  Usually, salmon has a nice fatty texture but that was completely gone.

2. Sweet Corn griddlecakes were good, with a nice light texture.  Eggs were standard.  Turkey sausage was not good -- dry & overcooked.

THE SERVICE was slow & difficult.  That is, it's difficult to get the servers' attention.

Place is very quiet and beautiful, but the food quality not so much, this place is pretty pricey and has small portions. I had the fried calamari as my appetizer, which was very sweet and drenched in the sweet and sour sauce. I had the Pad Thai as my entree. It was alright, I had better for cheaper. And had some of the Pad Si Ew, which was my least favorite. It did not look appetizing. It was served on a very big plate, with the food served all on one side of the big plate. The eggs were cooked in a way such that it looked like paste or non existent. Small portions and lots of unfinished food, just didn't enjoy the food. Overall, was not pleased with the foods. Reviews and pictures are very convincing on Yelp but I felt mehhh...

Tasty dishes, however very small portions.
Did not live up to its reputation.  Service  was sparse as well.

It's often so hard to find a good Mexican restaurant in philly in my opinion, or even just a good restaurant in general that doesn't serve tiny portions but still offers good quality food. This place was an exception. The service was great. We requested a more private table for our anniversary and that's exactly what we got. We had to call and give them a heads up because we were running about 15 min late and there were no problems with that either. We got there and were seated immediately, served drinks and food right away.. I think we were in an out of there within an hour. It's a little pricey but the food was definitely worth it... no tiny portions and great tasting food. My husband is half Ecuadorian so he's a snob with Spanish/Mexican food and we both agreed that this place was delicious. Drinks were strong, too, which is of course important!

(3.5 stars, really)

Tres tres francais, MAIS tres tres petit.

In other words, the flavors and the quality of the food were excellent and true to french cuisine.  Very well prepared and executed extremely beautifully.  HOWEVER, the restaurant and portions were extremely small.  What does this mean?

Small restaurant = feels like every other byob in philadelphia.  Cramped space, door to bathroom in the dining room which swing right open for a view of the toilet from the tables, and decor from ikea.

Small portions = $26 for 2 minuscule medallions of veal in my entree?   Please.  

I'm not a huge-portion type of person, but I also have a minimum threshold below which I find portion size to be ridiculous and offensive.

Had to go to whole foods afterwards and get a snack -- and this was after an appetizer, entree, and a shared dessert.

Please, please, 

Where is the delicious cream of crab for the crab fries. I was so , so, disappointed with the food from this restaurant. Nothing is what you would expect. Don't fall for the freshly made each order bull sh*t. The famous crab fries are minus crab and hard as rocks,loaded with salt and old bay so,  don't risk your health , trust me! This place is way over priced for the food and the drinks are watered down but, if your here for the game and a few shots they have great screens and so,so music. They are so sticking it to every one whom gets served here! You'd be better off going to red lobster to sea food differently....which up until my visit to chickies was a joke about there small portions, but if you really want small portions just order chickies & peas 3 crab cake entree ( not served with fries or salad) for $21.00  and awful tasting. Bone petite! Not!

Don't go hungry or you'll be disappointed; very small portions, expensive, but the food was good. Those who dined with me felt the same... they should really consider expanding the portion size. I didn't get to experience the jazz parlor; that is the only thing that would bring me back.

The once large portions seem to be a thing of the past, my most recent experience was disappointing. The dry pot was very small and contained about 5 measly pieces of each protein choice. What was once a shareable meal is now a personal sized pot.

We left hungry and had to go down the street and eat again.
Very flavorful, delicious food! Very large portions! The lady who works there is very nice and will give you suggestions if you are unsure what to get. Good bang for your buck!

Hubby and I had a craving for soul food today. Our close-by tried and true spot Aprons has sadly closed down, so I used Yelp to find something else near us. Soul Boat was fast and the prices are low for large portions, but I'd say the food was just decent. We ordered the fried catfish platter with Mac n cheese and collard greens and the fried chicken (leg and thigh) with Mac n cheese and string beans along with an extra side of rice and gravy. Pluses: not greasy, generous portions, varied menu. Minuses: lacked authenticity in flavors, veggies had no seasoning, rice was the same white rice used for Chinese food take out; instead of pleasantly marrying with the gravy, it just soaked it all up and was gummy. The catfish had a nice, light batter but not what I was expecting for soul food and the chicken was tender with a nice crispy coating but it wasn't a stand-out.

I ordered from Chowbus here, and the order was prepared quickly. Unfortunately, the flavor of the dishes left more to be desired. The only great dish I had here was the cold gluten - must get! Everything else - The scallion noodle and shanghai noodle were both a tad too oily and a bit bland - felt like it needed a little something more. The sauce in the sesame noodle was a bit too heavy handed with the peanut butter/sesame and could've used some diluting. I'm grateful that they have an option for vegetable dumplings, which was filled with a good portion of filling - however, this definitely lacked some flavor and needed a dipping sauce to complete it. However, great thing is that it's a good price for a good portion size and vegetarian options are available.

Zama is definitely my to-go place in Phili. Husband is living here. Almost go to Zama every time I'm in Phili. Tried couple of other Japanese restaurant here, but none of them is comparable to Zama. Understand people's complaints about the small portion. But this is not those pasta places where serve you huge portions of carb. It's a very interesting, full of thoughts, culture and innovation restaurant! 

Had the 75$ tasting menu today. 
It started with a fried fish/ seaweed salad. Not a big fan of the fried fish. A little too dry for me. But the dish had a good portion of vinegar which arouses your appetite!

The second dish was a lobster daikon roll. Absolutely loved it! The flavor is just about right! Refreshing and delicious.

Our third dish was a sashimi trio. It came with three sashimi and some dipping/ seasoning sides. The big chuck of salt was definitely the highlight..

Came here for nostalgia night for my first time here and it was so-so. The interior decor of this place though is super vintage and i felt like i was in an italian mob movie which was great.

I obviously came for the amazing prices but soon to discover the prices match the portions.

Calamari - very well cooked and honestly a good portion compared to the others.

Cesar salad - soooo heavily drenched in dressing and parmesan cheese but i know some people are into that sorto f thing

Carbonara pasta for 2 - good portion for 2 people to share and was pretty good; i love the spiciness to it!

Zuppa de pesce - too much fish not enough other seafood. and the fish has bones. the gravy was a bit salty... not the biggest fan of this dish

veal 3 ways - WAYYY over  cooked and too chewy, i barely touched this dish.

Stumbled upon this place while looking for a brunch spot in CC that didn't have a ridiculous wait at noon on a Sunday - great find! 

Tl;dr: trendy venue, generous portions for good prices, great for brunch w/ no wait.

Venue is open, brightly colored, and clean. Staff is reasonably friendly. Of note: they can only split a bill evenly, so if you want to pay separately, request separate checks.

To start, coffee is $3.50 for a bottomless cup - yay!!

They've got a good number of vegetarian options, and a few vegan options. Everything is $10-14 - reasonable prices for generous portions! The best dish, in my opinion, is the Chilaquiles Rojos/Verdes. It's the biggest portion for the least price ($10), and I really enjoyed the sauce (I ordered Rojo), and perhaps this is the nature of the dish but it does get soggy after a bit - I personally didn't mind it.

Noord has excellent service, a friendly chef, and large portions of properly cooked food.  So why only three stars you ask?  Well, it just wasn't for me.  The flavors were bland and the food was heavy, and this of course is not a cheap place to eat.  If I'm paying around $100 after tax and tip for two people, I want to leave thinking about amazing flavors.  That didn't happy here.

Now to be fair, I know absolutely nothing about Dutch food.  This was my first time giving it a go. Those who love heavy sauces and large portions of protein would probably love Noord.  My husband really enjoyed his meal here.  He had duck and was raving about it, and he was also happy with how stuffed he was when he left the restaurant.  

We both ordered the mustard soup with scallop as our appetizers.  This was my favorite of the evening.  The scallop was perfectly cooked, large, and tender.

Good food but it's too restaurant is too small. Generous portions. Wide variety of drinks available. Even the pickiest eater can find something to eat. However, with the restaurant being so small and the large plates gives it a claustrophobic feel to the place.

Lets cut to the chase, in addition to the bar tab, the "dinner" consisting of 1 beer, small plate of seafood mix, ribs ( at $9), suckling pig, pasta and dessert with 1 coffee...$110 w/tip. The "suckling pig" was a piece of pork, the volumetric size of a deck of cards (with good portion of fat) over beans, the mix was about 2 tablespoons full of seafood, the ribs were 3 small ones. The pork was $31. NOTE_ They tout this as a "sharing:" restaurant..How do you share 3 small ribs between 2 people? Don't go by the photos. If you get the camera close enough and use a small plate, it does look like you get a good portion. This place is for the "uber generation" who need to be seen. Personally, there a many places in the area offering better value to be "seen in". There are no drinks or food worth that money, $135 for 2 people. And if you want to spend a fortune just to "be seen" or name drop.
This is a great place.  The food is delicious and plentiful.  The people there are very nice.  Plus they have their own parking lot.

I really liked the layout of the restaurant. The menu was very good and the drink selection was great. It's nice that they have a parking lot next to the facility as street parking is tough. It's a bit pricey but it was well worth it.

Wifey and I visited this place on the way to an Eagles game last year, expecting to have some GREAT donuts, and GOOD chicken.  I was intrigued by the concept of a place that specializes in DONUTS and CHICKEN....not really two items you generally would put together, but certainly two of many peoples, myself included, favorites!  

This place ended up offering the exact opposite in my opinion; GREAT chicken, and GOOD donuts.  We got a half order of the Buttermilk Ranch seasoned "twice fried korean style" chicken, and I swear...I'm not like a chicken connoisseur or anything, and I haven't traveled the world 'round looking for the best chicken, but in my 30 years of life on this planet, it was the BEST I've ever tasted.  Perfect crispiness on the outside, just the right amount of seasoning without being too much, and the actual chicken itself was nice and hot, and flavorful.  Incredible!!
Delicious food and great service! Also has its own mini parking lot located on the side of the building if you have a car!

Let me just say that my favorite thing about this restaurant was admiring the beautiful mosiac on the wall, done by local artist Isaiah Zagar (South St. Magic Gardens). I was dissapointed when we were seated in the rear of the restaurant, which is not as visually interesting. We started with a few cocktails and an appetizer. The Tempura Veggies w/ Soy Ginger Dipping Sauce hit the spot. The vegetables were fresh and the tempura crispness on the outside was perfect. I love anything dipped in Soy Ginger, so this was my favorite part of the meal. I was in the mood for a good salad so I ordered the Blackened Salmon Salad. The Salmon was excellent... It was a nice sized piece and was blackened just right on the outside. Yummmmm. The rest of the salad was just plain. That's the best word I can use to describe it. It was pretty simple and came with an average vinagrette dressing.
Parking is hard & it gets very crowded in the restaurant & waiting area. Food was great but not worth the hassle!

From the moment you enter the doors to this restaurant you feel as though you are in a France. Our host Joshua showed us to our beautifully set table and offered to give us a tour of the restaurant and kitchen after we dined. The entire restaurant is run by students who attend to your every need. The service is superb. The restaurant is designed to make you feel as though you are eating in a Parisian cafe. Every detail from the babbling fountain , the dimly lit street lights, and perfectly balanced background music adds to the ambience. The tables were decorated perfectly , although the chairs were slightly uncomfortable. 

We started our meal with drinks that included a light refreshing Framboise spritzer made with grey goose vodka, chambord, lime , mint, and club soda and a Pome fume with gin and apple juice.  Next came deliciously fresh crisp French bread with homemade creamy butter.

Don't drive there as there is no place to park. The parking lot the restaurant says they have available turned us away full. They wouldn't seat our party until all guests arrived and I couldn't find a place to park in blocks and blocks of searching. We ultimately left without eating Uber or Lyft or taxi is the only option if driving.

I live 4 blocks away, so this is our go-to BYO, but our NYC friends say it is their Philly favorite now too. Warning: I am one of those people who always orders the same thing.  I know, I SHOULD order something other than the grilled shrimp, vegetables and the substitute vanilla rice, but every time I go I am reminded of just how fabulous this entree is!  Crisp, perfectly cooked shrimp, FRESH FRESH FRESH veggies and the vanilla rice, so aromatic and perfect. Fortunately for review purposes, my husband is a bit more adventurous and has tried pretty much everything on the menu.  "Can't say enough good things about Figs" pretty much sums up his experience too.  He even loved the vegetarian entree.  We like that you can always get extra flat bread to go with the hummus or the baked brie.

Fat Salmon has delicious sushi roll options, especially with their specialty roll, and I absolutely love that they have great vegetarian options! I booked a reservation on Fat Salmon the week of since we wanted to dine here on a Friday night and the place is a bit small. Upon getting seated, the tables were a bit close together, and a bit difficult to figure out how to put our winter jackets on the seats without feeling squished. However, service here was nice. The waitress was very kind, patient, and offered great recommendations. For my vegetarian choices, I got the Midori, Gaji-Ya, and Old School. The Midori is rather simple, but I find that simple is best. It's a bunch of different veggies, and you could just appreciate the different veggies (some are pickled!). The Old School and Gaji-Ya were also great, though the Old School was slightly better than Gaji-Ya.

Where are people supposed to park? They ripped out the lot and left 5 thousand people to fend for themselves. Way to go!
So needless to say I never got in..

Ill update my review if I actually find a place to park or they put in the new lot and I can get inside..

Parking is awful.
Takes too long. 
Dirty.
Service is bad. 
Expensive.
Not good. 

Did I sum it up for you?  If not:  GO SOMEWHERE ELSE!

Where do I start? First of all, I read all of the wonderful reviews about this restaurant. I had to try it. Perhaps it was because it was a Sunday night fixed tasting menu (Warning: Find out what is on the menu before you go. There are no substitutes.) . We arrived a few minutes early for our 5:30 reservation. The dining room was empty, but we were asked to wait outside; thank goodness it was warm. Once inside the small, unremarkable dining room, we were given water, then basically ignored; no bread no nothing until all of the others for the 5:30 seating had arrived. That took until close to 6 pm. Then the first dish came. It was some sort of trout Sashimi with chopped raw cucumbers, salad greens and too many Jalapenos. The dressing would have been tasty if it wasn't so salty (I use a lot of salt and this was too much for me.) and vinegary.

A staple for excellent Spanish food, period. You won't be disappointed with anything on the menu. The flavor and freshness of all your favorite traditional meals can be found here. Literally, something for everyone, including the rookies. Great portions accompanied by great prices make it more than worth it. Their desserts are also delicious so leave room if you can. 

The popularity of the restaurant is a double edged sword of sorts. Obviously, it's a good sign because the food is excellent. But it also means that the restaurant is usually pretty full and a bit noisy. However, it typically doesn't take long at all for the friendly staff to find you a table. Come here for a vibrant atmosphere full of delicious bites and good conversation.
Good cheesesteak - enjoyed the corner store ambience. Nice sociable owner, no wait and wide selection of sodas and drinks. Overall positive experience and good price!

Excellent food, service, and wine, in a very pleasant atmosphere. We sat in the enclosed porch with a nice view of greenery. They also have patio dining. We enjoyed halibut, ravioli, salads, and a dessert. All food was delicious and beautifully served. Wait staff was very amiable and efficient.

Lots of choices for vegan baked goodies, bagels, cream cheeses, milks for coffee, etc. It was a nice space with wifi and on-street parking (if you can find a spot). It's an older building in a residential area, but it feels cozy and I noticed  the staff  warmly welcoming their regulars. I got a mocha, bagel with cream cheese, and a chocolate cannoli. Everything was delicious!

This is a perfectly cozy, little place to have coffee, read a book, or work on your laptop! The setting is very nice. Service is friendly. I think the biggest thing I like about this place is the extra space upstairs for additional privacy (in the event that downstairs is crowded).

Food: 3
Service:3
Value: 3

Definitely not as good of an experience as the restaurant, but you can do worse with food trucks.

Came here with a friend this weekend after a recommendation from another friend. All employees were wearing masks. They informed us the wait was 45min-1hr but it ended up only being 20-25min. We were seated outside - half of the tables have umbrellas but we were seated at a table without one - this wasn't bad at first but as it got sunnier and warmer, it got a little uncomfortable. I wish they had more umbrellas available - try to get seated under an umbrella if you can.

I ordered the Crabby Dick on a biscuit after talking with the waitress and it was definitely a good call. It didn't look like much food at first but I ended up feeling super full and couldn't actually finish all of it. The potatoes looked really good but they were a little bland and had less seasoning than I expected. The biscuit was fluffy while with the crab cake was crispy - both delicious.

The food here was absolutely fantastic. I'd heard rave reviews about it from friends who live in the area and decided to stop by en route to D.C. not knowing that it was a fairly upscale restaurant. Due to it being the night before Valentine's, they were really booked up, but they were able to get my co-worker and I a table, so we could try it out. 

We had appetizers as well, and everything was superb. 
The ladies that run the place treated us like their favorite nephews. They were so friendly and welcoming. We were in military combat uniform heading home from training and felt badly being dressed down, but they asked us to stay and were so nice and brought the food quickly, so we could get back on the road. 

Prices are around the $15-35 range for most meals. 

This place would be ideal for a date night.
This place has great location and ambiance, the food and service was excellent, finding parking can be a little difficult but all in all it was a great experience
it is a really nice place, friendly atmosphere and food is delicious. But it is big problem with the parking we spend 30 min looking for place to park
Fantastic food!!! Wish there would be more space inside, and parking outside...but the marvelous taste of the food makes up for it all!
Great restaurant and exceptional food. The staff is courteous and helpful. Parking can sometimes be difficult and if you do find a spot watch the time, the PPA is merciless.

Everything is excellent here. The restaurant is very clean and the servers are very professional. You can pick anything on the menu and it will be great. The only problem is they have a very small parking lot. We like to go early in between lunch and dinner.

No parking around there and they are a holes about it. I was up for 20 hours and no parking anywhere so I ate at a place with parking lot. They wouldnt let me stay in parking lot. My airbnb is 2 blocks away and I could have walked. Why do they still give me a check with tip line? Clearly they dont care a rats ass about me. Why tip them? I offered to move after 4 hours it at 7 am. No one cared.

Pizza= eh. Needs more sauce. Like the soft crust but was kind of cold by the time it got to me. 

This review is about the delivery. WORST DELIVERY SERVICE I HAVE EVERY HAD. I get it, I live in the city, parking it sparse. But to be honest that isn't my issue. Do not call me and tell me to come meet you down on the street to pick up my order. Not only did my delivery person tell me to do that, I could barely understand a word he said because all he would repeat is "no parking, no parking" in a heavy Italian accent. Bro, I know there isn't parking, I just told you there's a valet zone you can put your flashers on right outside my building bring my pizza upstairs to my apartment and earn your 20% tip (AND DELIVERY FEE!!!) so I don't have to put a bra on and make myself look presentable. He hung up on me and ended up leaving my pizza at the front desk. So so rude.

New Town Deli and Restaurant is a little gem located in the no- man's land between Callowhill and Spring Garden Streets.  Clean and reasonably priced, New Town is a favorite breakfast and lunch place for the cops, cabbies, firefighters and government workers who work on Spring Garden Street.  Service is friendly, and the owners, who are Greek, have a firm grip on American Comfort food.  I have been to New Town several times for lunch, and always get the specials, which are delicious.  Today was the first time I ordered breakfast at the New Town, and it did not disappoint.  Breakfast for two, friendly service, and bottomless cups of coffee were less than $12.00.  
     There is no parking lot, and, at lunch time, parking on 9th street can be a challenge. No parking issues during our 7AM arrival for breakfast.

This park is like a mini get-away from city life. They have several options as far as trail systems for different activities. They have a long gravel road for easy bike riding/ running walking the dog and so on. They also have some pretty sick MTB trails that will test your skills and is a known hot spot for raiding in the city. You can get maps online for the MTB trail system. If you go to the opposite side of the creek there are really good hiking trails that are some what challenging at some points (rocky,steep). It's a really nice place just look out for no parking signs because PPA is always on the prowl on the weekends when it's hard to park.

Chickie and Pete's turned out to be a food truck that was closed anyway along with several other food trucks in Harbor Park - all closed - didnt open until 2:00pm.    We continued to walk down to the Mosholu only to find out they were only open for dinner .  
Keep in mind, due to a few health issues, Marianne cannot walk very far .  She is a trooper and did not complain at all but I knew I had to get her a bench or chair real soon.  It was pretty hot out and the wind just died.  
We then walked just a little more to The Chart House.  The parking lot was full and we knew we were going to eat and have our special drink to celebrate her great news.  We thought.  We opened the door, we were met by the General Manager, Michael, only to hear  The Chart House is only open for dinner.  The reason the parking lot was full is because there is a banquet going on.
Cozy ambiance and amazing food but no parking. Staff was very personable. Food was timely. It was a weeknight and not too busy. Check out my pics for details on the food:)

As to other issues, here is the run down: parking was available in a nearby free parking lot; the wait service was friendly and service was quick; the atmosphere was perfect for quiet two-person conversation and large group atmosphere; and the prices were moderate.

I highly recommend this restaurant.
At ~2 pm, NO wait for either a outside or inside the restaurant and free parking across the street.  And they were very "High Chair Friendly".  Because sometimes, thats just how I roll.
Everything was delicious and there's a parking lot on the right of the shop.
Food was delicious! Staff friendly, casual atmosphere. Parking wasn't even an issue - there's a parking lot down the street and off-street parking with Kiosks ($5 for a few hours) nearby.

I reserved the 4 upstairs lanes for my husband's surprise 30th birthday on 6/13

Location - we took the train down, and it was a super-easy shot from the Norristown Transportation Center - took the HSL to 69th, and MFL to Spring Garden - less than a 1/2 mile walk from there! Free parking is find-able, and all our guests found a place within a half mile as well - most of the free parking seems to be up on the corners of 2nd and Germantown.

Service - pretty much everyone was late because of Phillies/weekend traffic. They held the food until everyone was there, and gave us a FREE HALF HOUR at the end of the reservation to help out! How kind! The girl running the show was attentive and clear and helped pack up all the leftovers for our guests and us to take home! Which we did because the food was SO GOOD!

I didn't like it here at all. There's not many good things I can say about Fat Tuesday's. It's overpriced and they charged a $5 cover charge to get in. 

It's located on South Street near 5th Street. I would suggest taking an Uber here unless you're very patient or get here early in the day because free parking is all but impossible to find late night. There's a parking lot across the street, on the other side of the buildings but charges $20 for two hours to park. I wouldn't suggest even taking a chance to park somewhere on or around South Street because they were constantly writing parking tickets and towing cars.

Upon entering Fat Tuesday's, there were people gathered outside and there was a strong presence of weed as I walked in. I paid a $5 cover charge and entered. There wasn't a whole lot going on here. A lot of people sitting and standing around conversing with their friends.

I took my fiance last night for his birthday.  The only reason we came here was because our first choice had no openings for 3 hours and I'm glad we did. 

Being our first time, it was a bit confusing and we were lost, fortunately for us the waitstaff were impeccable and predicted all of our needs. We waited around an hour and had a few drinks at the bar. I had the brazilian Martini and mango refresco both very tropical tasting and strong. As others have mentioned, drinks are a bit pricer however I won't complain as they were strong and quality juices and ingredients were used. 

When our table for 2 was ready we were taken back. Wow does food taste better when you don't have a screaming and kicking toddler. Thanks mom! Our waitress took our drink order and explained the process. We understood the salad bar process and the green and red chip but were a little lost on the sides.

Listen ... this chicken ... Oh My Goodness! There are not enough words in the dictionary to explain how perfectly seasoned and tasty this rotisserie chicken is. This location is fairly close to work so I have only been around lunch time. I typically get the 1/4 chicken (you pick white or dark meat) with 2 sides. The sides i have tried are the Peruvian fried rice, white rice, black beans, string beans and the yucca fries and all have been on point. You cant beat the amount of food you get for the price ...and it tastes SO good! They also have a bunch of other options on the menu that I have yet to try but I'm sure they are just as good. 

If you get the chicken with the 2 sides its set up like assembly line style so you get in and out really quick. The other options on the menu they cook to order so it takes about 5-10 minutes around lunch time.

Great food and everytime I've benn there service has been decent. It's not a four start restaurant afterall so don't expect that, but still good. The food is amazing so what more can you ask for? Parking is hit or miss, so there are always 2-3 places we think of getting food close by, so that we are bound to get lucky with parking SOMEWHERE!

Small, intimate, fabulous food and great service.

Parking is promlematic, but the food and service make it worthwhile.
Good food!!! Parking lot!!! Ok service. Limited English staff so it's a point and nod kinda place.
Great place. Food is delicious and somehow always find parking tight in front. This is my lucky happy spot.

A great experience!   Very nice place. Tables spaced far enough that we didn't feel packed in. 

The service was impeccable. Polite, friendly and knowledgeable. Best service I've had in at least the last two years. 

Food, especially starters and dessert was great, as were drinks.  

And a real bonus: their own parking lot! A rarity in the city.

Food was delicious (as always). My only gripe is parking (limited in the area) and cleanliness. The other locations I've been to have at least one employee that goes through the restaurant and wipes down tables after each use and cleans up as needed. However, I didn't see one here. Other than that the staff were nice and our food came out in a timely manner.

We had a reservation for brunch for a party of 7 people. This place was quite happening, I really enjoyed the tunes they were playing in the background....it was very island inspired. The food was really good.

They have a brunch and dinner menu. The brunch one ends at 3pm. It's a vegan/vegetarian spot. The menu had a lot of flavorful choices. Can't really tell what countries the different dishes were from but there was fresh guacamole, plantains, tacos and also a variety of drinks from coffee to alcohol.

I had sweet plantains, which were great! It was 6 pieces and they weren't too soft or too firm, they were just right and sweet enough to hit the spot. I also had Cauliflower buffalo tacos, that were amazing! I was too hungry at the time but I wish I could eat them again. I aspire to make cauliflower tacos this well at home.

The parking sucks depending on what time of day you're shopping, the store not bad you can find what you're looking for, friendly enough if you're in the fast food section, the inventory staff were very helpful in telling you where to find what you need, most of the cashiers are nice and move quickly...then there is the group of employees that clusters in the front engaged in chit chat too long, with the amount of customers in the store daily from 11am to 8pm their should be more open registers, it's the only market in the area for half a mile in any direction, which is why the parking sucks, also you need to relocate the handicap parking and increase from the 6 spaces to 10 even at your peak times, there is security and that's good, but you have customers whom stop and wait in the front of the entrance, waiting for pick up and getting around them is ridiculous at times, you need a

My first time here was meeting friends for their Sunday Brunch.  I am used to a fixed price buffet brunch but soon discovered this was not that kind of place. Everything is ala carte.  We went for the "For the Table" special ($96) which is a 24 ounce dry aged Porterhouse steak with potatoes and 12 eggs. However the waiter said they ran out of it yesterday and did not have it for the Brunch service today. He then suggested we order several things and share items so we took his advice. 

First up was the Smoked Salmon Toast ($15). A generous portion of smoked Salmon arrived on 3 pieces of crustless toast. We cut each in half to get 6 pieces. It was very good and gave us all just a taste.

Next up was the pasta dish Tagliatelle ($16). It was delicious tasting but truthfully it was an embarrassingly small portion to share among 5 people.

THIS IS MY FAVORITE PHILLY CHEESESTEAK PLACE IN PHILLY!!!!

I would consider myself a local now. Transplanted from California, the land of the Foodies. I have tried a number of the philly cheesesteak places and this is why I like it (and others may have different tastes).

Texture of the meat: Tender beef cuts that maintain texture. Kind of like chinese hotpot beef, it keeps it's form, so when you bite into the sandwhich, you have some meat to chomp off. Other places have chopped up beef pieces, and that's not for me. Then, their cheese is interspersed in between the meat and it's great!

Toppings: I LOVE their mushrooms. Definitely get that if you love it. The texture and flavor of the mushrooms were so fresh. I now get a hoagie cheesesteak because I need the veggies to make a sandwich complete. I'm not a purest in that sense, but still know how to enjoy a good sandwich.

I grew up around this way. And always Drove by hear but never went in for breakfast, until today. But wish I would have years back. 

When I walked in I could only think how small the place is. But alot of seating. Very nice staff. 

The MENU has a huge selection of breakfast. With different specials for everyday. And most specials include the coffee. And when I say the prices are cheap I mean there cheap. Coffee and full breakfast for under $6, can't be beat. Won't find that around. 

I got the eggs, home fries, bacon, toast, coffee. 

Eggs over easy, done just right, bacon done perfect, coffee was good not bad, the toast I thought was alittle to burnt and was not cut. But its okay not going to complain over that. And the homefries are awesome a onion taste to them. Just how i like home fries. 

I will definitely be coming back hear for another good breakfast!!
Fabulous! First, parking wasn't a problem. That's a good start. The staff was polite and welcoming. Diners were safely spaced. Can't wait to go back!

Food and drinks were good, but DO NOT VALET HERE!!!! I did as they advised and requested my car via text 15 minutes prior to leaving out the restaurant.......40 minutes later and I am still waiting!!!! Makes for a very, very bad experience!! I will NEVER come back here because of the parking situation. Drivers BEWARE!

It was pretty good really nice atmosphere you would really have to plan to valet park your car if you want to drive. There are some Parking lots however it may be a little inconvenient.
I didn't really enjoy my black inch grout. It was a little dry however everyone else enjoyed their meal and we're happy. When I go there again maybe, maybe not.

So-so at best. 
Parking was an act of mercy not knowing where is allowed (legal) and where that you'd  end up on Parking Wars to get your car out of impound. Service was very slow for both drinks & food. Our server was far out...in left field. Fries were great! My wife's kale salad looked great. Very cool interior and bar/courtyard area. 50/50 as to going back.

Great ambiance snd menu. Will definitely come back

On arrival you can park on the street but half s block down there is a parking lot that you can pay $5 for 3 hours (as of 2021). Totally worth it to not stress about your car.

Restaurant has a relaxed and hip decor. Has some seats on sidewalk. We sat out back. It was a large are under a tent. Really quite lush. I was totally surprised!! We had advanced reservations on a Friday for lunch and it was busy but seats still available.

When sat we were told they automatically add 20% tip and there is a 90 minute max. Since it wasn't busy at 2pm and we were drinking steadily they didn't seem to care about the max time. If it was busy I'm sure they would do they could seat more guests.

Menu has lots of great healthy options and plenty that aren't. Breakfast served until 3 pm too!

My friends first arranged a small birthday dinner here for me before and it was fantastic. Since then, I've visted this place several times. The atmosphere is as relaxed as it gets with tasteful Latin music in the background. It can get a little packed here during the busy times as the first floor seating gets filled up quickly but there more seating upstairs where there is a larger bar. The food is authentic and delicious - and the presentation of plates are gorgeous. I love coming here for the happy hour now and then with several friends - especially for their long list of mojitos. The waiters are attentive and have interesting personalities. There's a lot of energy in this place when it's busy but it's not too loud that you can't comfortably speak with another person across from you. 

Pros:
Great selection and quality of mojitos, margaritas, and smoothies.
Good authentic food.
I think the food here is great! Service is also great! The only thing preventing me going there is the parking.

Good for pho.  Very satisfying.  They have a lot of seating and they're fast. 
Only problem is the parking lot can be a nightmare.

Loved this spot! I had heard so many great things about this place before going, and I was not disappointed.
